Name: Drip Filters - Kent Microlot
Desc: Processing: Naturals, Patio DriedVarietals Grown: Arabica ( Kent)Altitude: 1000 m.a.s.lRoast: Medium RoastFlavour Notes:Flavour Notes: ORANGE CANDY AND BERRIES. An aromatic coffee with balanced, sparkling acidity and a fine body. It is believed that the Kent variety roots back to the first Bourbon seeds brought out of Yemen to India by Baba Budan in 1670. It originates from a selection made by Mr. L.P. Kent in 1911 from a single tree growing in his Doddengooda Estate in Mysore, South Western India. It was widely planted in India since the 1930s and became very well known for its excellent flavour profile. Slowly, due to its susceptibility to many pests and diseases, the Indian farms made a switch to hardier varieties of Arabica and Robusta. Kogilahalla Estate is one among the few estates which has managed to retain its Kent coffee plants. These old plants are specially tended to and a micro lot of ripe fruits are selectively handpicked every year. The berries are then sun dried on raised beds after a short pre-fermentation phase. With its naturally high sugar content, the pre-fermentation step lends the coffee its complex winey notes that complements the syrupy body and enhances aroma. One can easily say that Kent, hands down, is one among the most splendid Indian varieties of Arabica Coffee.

Name: Drip Filters - Kogilahalla Estate
Desc: Kogilahalla Estate is named after the melodious cuckoos, known as “Kogile” locally, which inhabit the valley in which this pristine estate is found. The flora, fauna and the coffee of the estate co- exist in unison. Squirrels, Civet Cats, Porcupines can be found alongside the coffee plants. Meanwhile the estate comes alive to the sound of Hornbills, Kingfishers, Flowerpeckers and Flycatchers. The third generation owned family estate uses only the best natural methods of pest control which allows the flora, fauna and coffee to flourish. Processing: Anerobic Yeast Fermented, Patio DriedVarietals Grown: Arabica ( S795)Flavour Notes: PEACH, STONE FRUITS, TEA ROSE, MELLOW ACIDITY & FLORAL NOTESAltitude: 1000 mRoast: Medium

Name: Mysore Nuggets Extra Bold
Desc: Origin: North CoorgProcessing: Washed, Patio Dried.Roast: Medium to Dark  RoastVarietals Grown: Arabica ( S795) Flavour Notes: A well balanced cup with medium acidity & body, enhanced aroma and hints of chocolate & caramel.  This supreme grade of washed Arabica earned India its initiation into the Specialty Coffee Market. Mysore Nuggets Extra Bold, is a testimony to the efficacy of shade grown coffees in the Western Ghats of India.   It's a culmination of the best practices of agriculture combined with the forces of nature creating the most well developed bean the plant can offer.  The green beans of Plantation A Arabica meet the mark of being above 6.5 mm in size.  The Mysore Nuggets Extra Bold raises the bar,  90% is larger than 7.5 mm in size and 100% larger than 6.5mm. These beans are bagged by strict scrutiny of pre and post harvest processes which amounts to just 7 to 10% of the entire harvest. Physical Attributes - The beans are large and uniform, bluish-green in colour, and have a clean, well-polished appearance. They provide a highly uniform roast.  In the Cup - The flawless feature contributes to a well balanced cup. Medium body, medium acidity, smooth and lively on the palate. Can be served as a black coffee on a manual brew or makes for a great combination in an espresso blend.  Our Mysore Nuggets are sourced from our partner farms across Coorg.

name: Arabica Naturals
description: Ainmane's Arabica Naturals coffee is sustainably processed with minimal water to remove any under-ripe or overripe coffee cherries. The sorted cherries are sun-dried, hulled and roasted. The process retains maximum flavour and has a low carbon footprint.

name: Kudlur
description: S795 (Selection-795) is an important coffee cultivar, being one of the first strains of C. Arabica discovered to be resistant to coffee leaf rust (CLR).It is a selection of the Balehonnur Coffee Research Station in India. S795 cultivar was developed by crossing C. Arabica (Kent Coffee) and C. Liberica. It is high yielding and has a good cup profile, making it a desirable cultivar for coffee planters. We have selected our beans from the Kudlur Estate, situated at an elevation of nearly 700M, in Somwarpet Taluk in Coorg

name: Anaerobic Naturals
description: Ainmane's Anaerobic Naturals Coffee cherry has undergone fermentation in sealed tanks to develop distinct acids that create its unique fruity flavor profile. The coffee is then dried in a natural process.

name: Robusta of Coorg
description: In the eventual movement of coffee planters opting to grow Robusta more than Arabica due to easier maintenance of the plantations, Robusta is extensively grown around Coorg compare to Arabica. This is purely shade grown coffee where the plantations eco systems are bordering the natural reserve forests which allow animals to roam freely around the plantations. This not only contributes in conserving wildlife, but has a whole, animals and insects play a vital role in maintaning the the bio diversity in plantations. Europe alone imports alone 30,000 tonnes of Robusta from Coorg annually. So the next time you on a Euro trip and sipping Coffee you might be served coffee from similar beans.

Name: Single Pour Drip Bags
Desc: For us, it’s all about sharing our roasts with you without the need for any equipments or fuss. Drip bags make it easier than ever-perfect for anyone craving pure flavour and convenience, or for those who need their coffee on-the-go. Just follow the below steps to brew one satisfying cup at a time: Step 1: Tear along the perforation. Step 2: Pull the flaps out and hang onto the cup. Step 3: Boil 180ml of water. Rest boiling water for about 1 min before pouring. Pour 30ml of hot water to soak the coffee and let it bloom for 30s. Slowly pour another 150ml. Step 4: Let it rest until 2 mins before removing the bag. Qty: 11g per bag / 6 drip bags in a pack Indicative flavour notes: We can’t tell you what you’ll taste because every palate is different. name: Pocket Brew – Collection
description:
From soil to cup, ARAKU is defined by its terroir—the unique combination of soil, climate, and altitude that gives our coffees their distinct character. With the Pocket Brew Collection, we’ve captured that story in elegant, single-serve drip bags you can brew anywhere. No grinder, no scale, no complicated equipment—just pure specialty coffee, simplified.

Inside each box, you’ll experience three of ARAKU’s celebrated terroir-driven coffees:

Selection – smooth and balanced, perfect for everyday moments

Micro Climate – nuanced layers that reflect the diversity of our valley

Grand Reserve – rich, indulgent, and crafted for special occasions

Whether you’re discovering specialty coffee for the first time or you’re a seasoned enthusiast seeking a travel-friendly solution, the Pocket Brew Collection makes it effortless to taste, compare, and choose your favorite ARAKU cup. Each drip bag is designed for consistency, freshness, and convenience—so you can enjoy café-quality coffee in just a few minutes.

More than just a coffee kit, this collection is also a thoughtful gift. Presented in a beautifully designed, premium box, it’s perfect for colleagues, friends, and loved ones who appreciate craft, sustainability, and the joy of sharing great coffee.

What’s Inside: This pack contains 15 single-serve coffee sachets — 5 each of Micro Climate, Selection, and Grand Reserve.

name: Pocket Brew - Selection
description:
If you’re just starting your journey into specialty coffee, or you're someone who loves great coffee even while traveling, the ARAKU Coffee Pocket Brew Selection is made just for you.

Inside each pack, you’ll find 10 single-serve drip bag sachets filled with freshly ground Selection beans from ARAKU Coffee. These sachets are nitrogen-flushed to lock in freshness, aroma, and flavor until the moment you brew. Just tear one open, place it over a sturdy cup, pour in hot water, and enjoy barista-quality coffee—anytime, anywhere.

Whether you're commuting, flying, road-tripping, or simply need a quick fix at home, this is specialty coffee made simple.

Perfect for Travel & Everyday Life

  • Lightweight and compact—fits in your bag, purse, or carry-on

  • No need for coffee gear—just a cup and hot water

  • Ideal for flights, hotels, hikes, or busy mornings

Great Coffee, Made Simply

  • Filled with 100% organic ground Selection beans from ARAKU Coffee’s tribal farmer community

  • Nitrogen-flushed to preserve freshness and flavor with every cup

  • Created for people new to specialty coffee or looking for a simpler way to enjoy it

name: Pocket Brew - Grand Reserve
description:
Our single-serve coffee packs combine the speed of an instant brew with the unrivalled quality of ARAKU's specialty coffee. As the name suggests, these drip bag sachets fit any pocket or purse and offer an extremely portable coffee. Each sachet is packaged individually and nitrogen-flushed to maintain the coffee's integrity and freshness. Suited for the airplane, the open road, hotels, offices, or even when you just need a quick fix at home. A sturdy cup and hot water does the trick.  

This pack contains 10 individual sachets.

name: Taste the Terroir: Coffee Sampler Pack
description:
In specialty coffee, flavour begins long before roasting — it begins in the land.

This Terroir Coffee Sample Pack is an invitation to explore how altitude, soil, micro-climate, and careful cultivation shape what you taste in the cup. Each coffee in this set comes from a distinct growing environment, allowing you to experience how terroir expresses itself through sweetness, acidity, body, and aroma.

Curated for both discovery and comparison, this set lets you brew the coffees side by side, slow down, and understand your own preferences — before choosing a larger pouch.

The collection includes four 100% Arabica coffees:

Selection – Medium Dark Roast
Rounded and balanced, with deeper body and comforting sweetness

Signature – Medium Roast
Smooth and versatile, designed for everyday clarity and balance

Grand Reserve – Medium Roast
Layered and refined, highlighting complexity and structure

Micro Climate – Medium Roast
Nuanced and expressive, shaped by specific micro-regional conditions

Roasted to highlight origin character rather than bitterness, each coffee reflects ARAKU’s commitment to traceability, craft, and flavour clarity.

Ideal for mindful brewing, thoughtful gifting, or anyone looking to deepen their understanding of specialty coffee — one cup at a time.

Desc:
Elevation: 1550 MASL

Variety: SL9

Processing: Washed

Roast: Medium

Producer: Govind ER

Tasting notes: Sweet Cherry, Bakers Chocolate, Honey

The Greenland Estate is nestled in Valparai, Tamil Nadu, within the dominion of the Anamalai Tiger Reserve. This region primarily thrives as a tea-growing region, though coffee is gradually gaining ground. Encompassing 200 acres, the estate is perched at an elevation ranging from 5100 ft to 5700 ft above sea level, a uniquely lofty position that imparts exceptional qualities to its coffee beans.

Derived from meticulously handpicked SL9 cherries, this washed processed coffee undergoes a meticulously crafted journey. Following a careful pulping process, the cherries are placed within specially designed fermentation tanks, where they rest for 16-18 hours. Subsequently, the seeds embark on a deliberate slow-drying process on raised beds for a span of 10-14 days.

The medium roast profile that we have crafted encapsulates the best of both realms. This coffee retains its distinctive sweet citrus acidity and the captivating floral notes that enamoured us upon our initial encounter. Simultaneously, it introduces a lasting and comforting essence of baker's chocolate and raw honey, creating a special balance of flavours. This unique composition yields a remarkable coffee experience, effortlessly adaptable to manual brewing or as an espresso, and equally delightful when enjoyed black or with milk.

Name: Venkids Valley Estate - The Red Honey - Light Roast
Tasting_Notes:
Mango, Hibiscus and Butterscotch

We along with so many others have swooned for two seasons over the incredible Yellow Honey that Pavan produces every year. This year, the team at the Venkids Valley Estate decided to take their Catuai a step further, from a Yellow Honey
Desc:
Elevation: 1000 MASL

Variety: Catuai

Processing: Red Honey

Roast: Light

Producers: Mr Pavan Nanjappa

Tasting notes: Mango, Hibiscus and Butterscotch

We along with so many others have swooned for two seasons over the incredible Yellow Honey that Pavan produces every year. This year, the team at the Venkids Valley Estate decided to take their Catuai a step further, from a Yellow Honey process to a Red Honey process and take our word for it, this is an exceptional coffee. With the new process, the coffee has become slightly sweeter with more intense flavours and a richer mouthfeel.

We have roasted this pretty lightly to let the coffee, and the process really shine through and take the centre stage. With sweet notes of Mango, rich butterscotch and delicate hints of Hibiscus this coffee makes an incredible filter coffee that we're sure you'll absolutely enjoy!

Name: Pulney Coffee (Washed) - Pulney Hills - Medium Roast
Tasting_Notes:
Citrus Fruits, Cherries, and Nuts

Originating from one of the highest growing regions in Tamil Nadu, these coffees are dense and have a beautiful aftertaste because of the high growing Region. The Laks farm is completely organic and devoid of any chemical pesticides and fertilisers. The coffees are intercropped with oranges, cardamom, pepper and banana. The beans of the highest brix are identified (colour coded bands are given to workers at the estate to pick the cherries). They are sorted for defects twice before using the penagos washer + pulper. Floats are removed and the coffee beans with little bit of mucilage are dried on raised beds. They are exposed to the morning sun for the first two days and then completely dried in shade for a period of 20-25 days.

Mr. Iyer is without doubt one of the sweetest and most earnest people we have encountered in coffee and with passion and efforts of Viggnesh in processing, this coffee was one of the best washed coffees we tasted this year! This medium roast has sweet notes of Cherry, and Nuts with a mild Citrus Acidity, and works really well both black and with milk, as a filter or an an espresso!

Name: Venkids Valley Estate (Washed) – Coorg - Medium Dark Roast
Tasting_Notes:
Mexican chocolate, Caramel, and Orange Zest

A short, scenic drive from Madikeri, past a rivulet or two, leads you to the charming “Papakuchi Coffee” by Venkids Valley Estate, where you are welcomed by Pavan and his wife Shilpa. The estate spreads across 200 acres, and is divided into “Patte” or fields, named aptly by the workers. Imagine being able to spot the exact patch of land your coffee was grown on. Yes, that’s the level of traceability Pavan is able to achieve at this estate.

This SLN6, grown in the “Kenjipatte” is roasted to slightly darker than a medium (some might even call it a medium) to really enhance the syrupy body and the notes of caramel which are offset by the a splash of orange zest. Pretty great for filters, great for espresso!

Pick you grind and brew away!

Name: Vin Van Gogh - Medium Roast
Tasting_Notes:
Berries, almonds, and spiced Chocolate

The origin of this blend goes a fair way back to when Pavan (Venkids Valley Estate) and Navin (Moganad Estate) were schoolmates and were busy making plans for the world domination of Indian speciality coffee! Little did they know then, that the catalyst for this would be small roastery out of Chandigarh, of all the places who would put their two phenomenal washed arabicas together in a top secret ratio, name it after the one of the greatest painters of all time, which is also a word play on their names, and make it the most the delicious, versatile blend to have ever come out of the greater Chandigarh region! Pavan and Navin still remain very tight, and share flights, coffees, jokes, and the roasters they choose to work with! Thankfully, they both agreed to partner with us, which in turn enabled us to come up with this super tasty, bright like a Red Vineyard, over The Cafe Terrace at night, lit up by The Starry Night

All stories aside our Vin Van Gogh is our answer to a coffee blend that does everything very very well! It makes a great fruity filter coffee, as well the perfect espresso to have as it is, or a lovely fluffy cappuccino! Pick the grind of your choice, and bask in the glory of Vin’s and Van’s artistry!

Name: Ro-Busta Rhymes - Dark Roast
Desc:
Elevation: 3300 ft. – 4500ft.

Varietal: Arabica S795, Robusta

Planters: Navin Rajes, and Pavan Nanjappa

Processing: Washed Arabica and Naturals Robusta

Roast: Medium Dark

This blend features the lovely washed arabica from the Moganad Estate, and the natural processed robusta from the Venkids Valley Estate. But beware, if you’re expecting a bitter, boring blend, this will let you down! Ro-Busta Rhymes is a super duper tasty blend that really brings the best out both species of the coffees, but what’s really interesting is that acidity and the sweetness in this blend comes a great deal from the Robusta! We recommend you try this blend black just to really get a feel of what the robusta brings to it!

Name: Satchmo - Dark Roast
Tasting_Notes:
Chocolate, Dark Caramel, and hints of Citrus

Chocolate, Dark Caramel and hints of citrus, sounds to us like one of the magnificent trumpet solos of the one the only Louis Armstrong! For us, Louis Armstrong a.k.a. Satchmo is the epitome of balance, with a voice that can go from a deep, rich gravel to almost fragile falsettos. Every moment of every song is filled with gorgeous melody, depth and genius improvisations!

“Satchmo” the blend, just like it’s muse, has pitch perfect sweetness, a deep body that swells like a crescendo, and a subtle “Vibratoesque” citrus acidity. A coffee that goes not toe to toe, but “Cheek to Cheek” with all accompaniments. The blend is on the darker side of a medium, and has the richness of chocolate and dark caramel, and a raspy acidity that can cut through whatever you throw at it, yes we’re looking at you milk and sugar. Satchmo makes the perfect espressos, moka pots, french presses, south indian filters, and what not, to get you a coffee that’ll make you see sit across and think “What a Wonderful World”

Satchmo is the epitome of balance, with a voice that can go from a deep, rich gravel to almost fragile falsettos. Every moment of every song is filled with gorgeous melody, depth and genius improvisations!

“Satchmo” the blend, just like it’s muse, has pitch perfect sweetness, a deep body that swells like a crescendo, and a subtle “Vibratoesque” citrus acidity. A coffee that goes not toe to toe, but “Cheek to Cheek” with all accompaniments. The blend is on the darker side of a medium, and has the richness of chocolate and dark caramel, and a raspy acidity that can cut through whatever you throw at it, yes we’re looking at you milk and sugar. Satchmo makes the perfect espressos, moka pots, french presses, south indian filters, and what not, to get you a coffee that’ll make you see sit across and think “What a Wonderful World”

Name: Meera - Medium Light Roast
Tasting_Notes:
Caramel, Bakers Chocolate, Berries and Vanilla

Meera - A fearless espresso blend that breaks the conventions of what an espresso blend should be! Meera is our Medium-light roast espresso blend with notes of strawberries, baker’s chocolate, vanilla and decadent caramel. This is our tribute to one of India's most celebrated mystic poets, Meera Bai.

Meera features two incredible coffees, our staple washed arabica from Coorg’s favourite plantation, the Venkids Valley Estate, and a stunning “Natural Naturals“ from the Krishnagiri Estate, located in some of the highest elevations of Chikmagalur. What do we get when we blend a clean bright washed and a super sweet, jammy Natural Naturals? A yummy, sweet, super complex, rich espresso, which holds its own in milk beverages as well!

It’s fair to say that this blend has had a pretty long development phase, but you know that we don’t take our blends lightly, and launch them only when we’re really happy with it, and right now we’re delighted with this and are finally ready to introduce you to “Meera”.

Recommended recipe:

Dose: Being a lighter roast, we would recommend dosing one-half a gram lesser than what you would dose for a medium/medium dark roast coffee

Grind Size: Grind a step or two finer than what you would normally for a medium roast

Yield: We recommend a yield of 2.5 times the dose of the dry coffee. For eg: Dose: 20 grams; Yield: 50 grams

Time: The lighter the roast, the more you need to extract to get good sweetness and complexity. We like shots between 28-33 seconds for a straight 9-bar approach for Meera. If you can pressure profile, we like to start with a 5-second pre-infusion at 2 bars, and then ramp up to 8 bars till we hit the desired yield, which usually takes around 45-50 seconds.

PUCK PREP: We can't over-emphasise how important the puck prep is for a coffee like this. Make sure, you dose correctly and evenly, WDT is highly recommended here, tamp as evenly as you can and clean around the edges of the portafilter. This will minimise channelling and give you a more even extraction.

Tasting_Notes:
Coffee Blossom, Stone Fruit, & Oranges

The Hoysala Estate was started in the late 1800s is has been family-owned since the 1950's. This washed
Desc:
Elevation: 1050 MASL

Variety: Sachimore

Processing: Washed

Fermentation: In fruit fermentation before pulping

Roast: Light

Producers: Hoysala Coffee

Tasting notes: Coffee Blossom, Stone Fruit, & Oranges

The Hoysala Estate was started in the late 1800s is has been family-owned since the 1950's. This washed process lot comes from their farm located in Angadi village near Chikmagalur where the Hoysala Dynasty started in the 9th century. Sunil & Mohan and their families have taken Hoysala coffee to similar heights through their incredible knowledge and expertise in growing, and processing coffee. Working with them for the first time during this harvest, and trying some of their coffees really blew us away.

Like other coffees at their farm, this washed coffee is grown using regenerative farming practices, and no chemical fertilisers. This fermented-washed Sachimore was one of our favourite washed coffees from the previous year's harvest and features a delicate floral note reminiscent of coffee blossom. With a medium-light roast, the coffee has developed a lovely stone fruit sweetness and a subtle orange acidity.

This coffee works superbly as a filter and as an espresso, and pairs very well with small milk beverages like a cortado or macchiato. We hope you love this one as much as we have!

Name: Anai Kadu - Naturals - Coorg - Light Roast
Tasting_Notes:
Plum, Bakers Chocolate & Orange

Anai Kadu takes its name of the Elepahants (Kadu) that frequent their estate. Located in Maldare in Coorg, Nisha and Kurian left their corporate lives in Bangalore and moved to their 50 acre coffee farm during the pandemic and started their journey of producing speciality coffee. Anai Kadu came to the fore a couple of years back when they did some incredible nano lots of their arabicas and robustas. Over the last few years,they established themselves as one of the more experimental and promising coffee farms in Coorg. From their gorgeous packing and hand-drawn illustrations that are sent with the green coffee samples to the meticulous farming and processing, they are one of the farms that we look forward to working with every year! Like last year, we picked up their Naturals, called the Elephant's Trail, but this time around it's an Aerobic Naturals which we really enjoyed and felt that it was a worthy repeat season ticket offering!

The Aerobic fermentation done with this S795 has yielded a super sweet and a fruity cup, without any booziness. We always enjoy sweet, and clean naturals, and this one is just that. Compared to some of the other coffees we've put out this year, this one is heavier on the mouthfeel and has a lovely chocolate finish. To enhance the syrupy mouthfeel, we roasted this a bit slower but kept is slight still. The coffee has a sweet plum flavour, with notes of citrus and syrupy chocolate finish.

This blend features the lovely washed arabica from the Salawara Estate, and the natural processed robusta from the Kottaram Estate in Wayanad, Kerala. This is the first time we've purchased coffee from Kerala, and thanks the incredible work and efforts done by Vinay, his family and his team at the estate, we were blown away by the flavour profile of the robusta naturals. Name: Udaigiri Estate - Honey - Chikmagalur - Light Roast
Tasting_Notes:
Stone Fruit, Red Apple, Malt

This fruity honey processed coffee from the Udaigiri Estate has been one of the coffees that we have been really looking forward to put out and we couldn't think of a better coffee to kickstart the new year. A clean, bright, fruity coffee, with the hopes of a bright, fruitful new year!

This honey processed coffee was grown at an elevation of 1250 MASL, and once the cherries were bright red and ripe they were harvested, cleaned, and fermented in open environment for 48 hours, while being carefully monitored and raked. They were then pulped precisely to leave a specific amount of mucilage to bring out the fruity notes that we love with a honey processed coffee and were dried for 22 days on raised beds.

We roasted this light to retain it's bright flavour, and bring out the sweetness of Red Apple, fresh stone fruit acidity, all balanced with a malt-like finish.

Desc:
Elevation: 1100 MASL

Variety: S795

Processing: Red Honey

Fermentation: 72 hours Anaerobic fermentation

Roast: Light

Producers: Sharan Gowda

Tasting notes: Amla, Kinnow & Jaggery

As many of you might know, Sharan was one of the first farmers we ever bought coffee from, in fact he was the first planter we ever met in real life! Back then Salawara Estate was just starting their speciality coffee journey, but in the last five years, they have undoubtedly emerged as one of the most outstanding coffee producers in the country. Their steadfast focus on agriculture and improving their infrastructure rather than content creation has yielded incredible results, and we're the ones reaping the benefits!

This year we purchased four lots from them, but this Anaerobic Red Honey was by far our favourite when we cupped it, and with the final roast profile, it's one of the juiciest coffees we have tasted in a while! This S795 grown at 1100 MASL was the last batch of coffee that was processed last year, and the slow maturation, with a higher mucilage content made this the perfect bunch for an Anerobic Red Honey Process. The Cherries were pulped lightly, leaving a lot of the mucilage and were then fermented Anaerobically for 72 hours before they were slow dried for 22 days. The cherries and the process produced a very fruit forward cup, high in sweetness and acidity.

To accentuate this, we roasted this super light, and the result is a super juicy coffee with notes of Blackberries, Orange Zest and a lingering sugarcane sweetness.

Name: Winter Blend
Desc:
Meet the blend our roasters look forward to crafting each winter. Pairing well with milk, it is also a solid base for all those winter recipes you've been saving.

We've created it using a careful mix of natural and washed lots from St. Joseph Estate and Attikan Estate. Opening with the aroma of brown spices, this coffee has a medium body and a syrupy, round mouthfeel. You’ll be able to taste cinnamon, cacao, roasted almonds, and raisins, and tying everything together nicely is a chocolatey aftertaste.

We recommend brewing it as an espresso, or with a Moka Pot or French Press.

We've created it using a careful mix of natural and washed lots from St. Joseph Estate and Attikan Estate. Opening with the aroma of brown spices, this coffee has a medium body and a syrupy, round mouthfeel. You’ll be able to taste cinnamon, cacao, roasted almonds, and raisins, and tying everything together nicely is a chocolatey aftertaste.

We recommend brewing it as an espresso, or with a Moka Pot or French Press.

Recommended Resting Period: 10 Days

Name: Half - Caff
Desc:
Our first-ever single-origin, specialty Half-Caff comes from Yelnoorkhan Estate. We selected their S795, washed processed coffee to create a complex and distinctive cup.  

To reduce caffeine by 55%, we used CO₂ decaffeination, a chemical-free, minimal-waste generating method that is conscious in its water and energy usage. We chose it because the other decaffeination methods available to us in India came with a catch. In removing all the caffeine, they also took away the depth that makes a cup memorable. Adding artificial flavours was not something we wanted to do, never mind the fact that many of these methods also used far too much water.  

The result is a cup with a gentler kick that holds its own in terms of flavour. You’ll first notice chocolate biscuits on the nose as well as your palate. A silky mouthfeel then reveals notes of roasted hazelnuts and malt, followed by a long, nutty finish. 

For the best experience, brew this coffee using an espresso machine. It tastes great black and is equally suited to milk-based beverages.

Recommended Resting Period: 5 Days

Note: This coffee pack is a special release with limited availability and, therefore, cannot be included in a subscription plan.

Name: Krishnagiri Estate
Desc:
A single origin dark roast, this coffee comes from a Rainforest Alliance Certified farm. The producers used a custom-designed pulper to process this washed lot, minimising water usage.  

In the cup, you'll first notice the aroma of brown spices. The brew, characterised by mellow acidity, a heavy body, and a velvety mouthfeel, reminds of oak, toasted walnuts, and malt. A bittersweet finish lingers between sips.  

We recommend brewing this coffee as an espresso, using a Moka Pot, French Press, or an AeroPress. It is rich enough to enjoy black, and also pairs well with milk.

Recommended Resting Period: 7 Days

Desc:
Meet the first coffee from our newest partner farm, run by a community of Jesuit priests whose stewardship of the land spans generations. 

A washed coffee roasted medium-dark, it opens with warm brown spice aromatics. Each sip carries a syrupy mouthfeel and reminds of grapefruit, clove, and toffee. Its medium-high body gives the cup a comforting depth, complemented by a chocolatey aftertaste. 

Our roasters recommend brewing it as an espresso, or using an AeroPress, Moka Pot, or French Press. A versatile brew, it pairs well with milk, and holds its own black.

Recommended Resting Period: 10 Days

Name: Monsoon Malabar AA- Hoysala Estate
Desc:
We’re excited to bring back Monsoon Malabar from Hoysala Estate. The unique flavour profile of this coffee develops when winds and humidity from seasonal monsoon rain change the characteristics of the coffee beans. While this process has its accidental roots in colonial India when a shipment to Europe was attacked by the full force of monsoon winds, similar conditions have been recreated in a controlled environment for consistency in every lot produced. 

When roasted medium dark, the result is a medium-bodied cup that invites with sweet aromas of butter biscuits, treating you to notes of cocoa nibs and dried fruit, concluding with the aftertaste of dark chocolate. Best enjoyed when brewed as an espresso, in the Moka Pot or the French press, the nutty flavour profile of this coffee makes for a delicious cup, either milky or black. 

Recommended Resting Period: 15 Days

Name: Dhak Blend
Desc:
Our Dhak Blend is an ode to one of our favorite Indian trees with its colorful flame-like flowers that signal the onset of Spring. The coffees used in this blend are naturally processed which means that the coffee beans are dried with the cherry, resulting in complex, fruity and sweet flavours.

Roasted dark to bring out flavours of dark chocolate and fruit jam, this blend's heavy cocoa body leaves a smooth lingering aftertaste.

Our roasting team recommends the Dhak Blend for espresso-based drinks as well as manual brews such as the Moka Pot and the French Press.

Name: Attikan Estate
Desc:
Attikan Estate's arabica coffee beans come from the Biligiriranga Hills in Karnataka and is make for one of our most popular coffees. Sweet with fruity overtones and balanced acidity, this is the darkest of our standard medium roasts and recommended for espresso lovers. It is a versatile coffee that also works for manual brewing such as Moka Pot, South Indian Filter and AeroPress. 

Located to the south of Mysore, the Biligiriranga Hills, or ‘white hills’ are named after the mist that hangs over the region. At 1650 meters, it is amongst the highest coffee growing regions in India and grows Selection 9, Selection 795, Cauvery and Kent varieties of Arabica, along with Silver Oaks, citrus, and fig trees.

Name: Basankhan Estate
Desc:
We are thrilled to present our first ever single origin dark roast, with coffee beans sourced from a new partner farm— Estate in Chikmagalur, Karnataka. 

This coffee has a journey of rich, complex flavours that will leave you craving for more. As you take a sip, enjoy the velvety mouthfeel reminiscent of dark chocolate, which enhances the overall richness of this brew. The coffee’s body is heavy and round, creating a luscious and full-bodied experience that envelops your palate. If you’ve liked our dark roasts like Vienna and Dhak, you’ll love this one! 
The Basankhan Estate is a family-owned farm located in Chikmagalur, Karnataka with a rich history spanning over 100 years. In addition to coffee, the estate cultivates other crops such as black pepper, oranges, cardamom, lemons, and bananas.

Name: Amaltas Blend
Desc:
An ode to the vibrant burst of yellow that marks the beginning of Indian summers, this blend is our go-to choice for crafting a refreshing batch of coffee including cold brews. In fact, this was originally called the Cold Brew Blend but owing to its diversity (its flavours shine through in a Pour Over or Aeropress), we decided to rename it after one of our favourite neighbourhood trees. 

A blend of washed and natural processed coffees, we’ve roasted it light to accentuate fruity and refreshing citrus notes. The result? Balanced cups with notes of blueberry and milk chocolate, with each sip concluding with a chocolatey finish.  

This light and fruity favourite is best enjoyed black.

Name: Mooleh Manay Estate – CM Natural
Desc:
Returning to our Producer Series after 2023, Komal Sable and Akshay Dashrath share their first experiment with carbonic maceration. Building on the clarity and consistency they achieved with anaerobic fermentation last season, the fifth-generation producers modified their drums to create a CO₂-rich, oxygen-free environment that allows for slower, more controlled fermentation within whole cherries. 

The process began by removing floaters to select only ripe, dense cherries, followed by a brief pre-drying phase to reduce surface moisture. The cherries were then sealed in drums, and a custom culture was introduced to extend the fermentation. Over 60 hours, this combination of carbonic maceration and yeast inoculation ensured thorough mucilage breakdown and the development of deep complexity. 

Post-fermentation, the cherries were dried on raised beds inside a polyhouse. Continuous raking over 7 to 10 days ensured even drying until a final moisture level of 11–12% was reached. 

Roasted light by Rishab from our team, this coffee offers a well-structured cup with notes of fermented red fruit and a bright, juicy sweetness. It opens with the aroma of mixed berries and carries a syrupy mouthfeel, with layered flavours of dried fig, plum, black grape, and mulberry. A chocolatey aftertaste marks the finish, adding further depth. 

We recommend brewing this expressive coffee black, as a Pour Over, or using an AeroPress.

Recommended Resting Period: 16 Days

Note: This coffee pack is a special release with limited availability and, therefore, cannot be included in subscription.

Name: 13th Birthday Blend
Desc:
This celebratory blend brings together natural lots from Stanmore, Orchardale, and Riverdale Estates in Yercaud, along with a washed lot from Unakki Estate in Chikmagalur, which forms the base. Its flavour profile takes us back to the Black Forest cakes many of us celebrated birthdays with during our teen years. 

Opening with the aroma of honey and strawberries, the cup has a medium-high body and a round mouthfeel. You'll notice notes of strawberry, chocolate, cherry, and pear, followed by a lingering finish of chocolate-covered strawberries. 

This blend brews well across a range of methods, including espresso, AeroPress, French Press, Moka Pot, and Pour Over. Equally enjoyable black or with milk, it lends itself to a wide range of recipes.

Recommended Resting Period: 10 Days

Name: SKIA Coffee (Pack of 2)
Desc:
This two-pack (100 gms each) brings together distinct coffees from Nelaji Village in Coorg. Grown by smallholder farmers and processed by Ashish Rao, a first-generation producer, these lots mark our first collaboration with Skia Coffee. 

Ripe, high-density cherries were pulped with the mucilage left intact, then placed in sealed tanks for a 72-hour anaerobic fermentation. A yeast strain purpose-built for controlled fermentation was introduced during this stage to develop complexity. 

From there, the two lots took separate paths. 

Honey Sun Dried  

The first lot was dried slowly on raised beds under controlled shade. Roasted to a medium profile, it makes for a balanced cup with notes of sweet lime, prunes, and almond. 

Recommended Resting Period: 16 Days

Thermal Shock  

This second lot was immersed in hot water, then rapidly cooled in ice. It was then mechanically washed and dried slowly under shade. Also roasted to a medium profile, it brews cups with notes of tangerine, brown sugar, and berries.  

Both coffees brew beautifully as an espresso or with an AeroPress, Moka Pot, or French Press. They taste great black and pair well with milk. Together, they offer a chance to explore how thoughtful shifts in processing shape flavour in the final cup.  

Recommended Resting Period: 12 Days

Note: This coffee pack is a special release with limited availability and, therefore, cannot be included in subscription.

Name: Warsanlyngdoh Coffee Collective
Desc:
It's always exciting for us to partner with a new farm. With Meghalaya's Warsanlyngdoh Coffee Collective, that excitement runs even deeper. A completely new coffee growing region for us, it speaks of the possibilities that the North East Indian soil holds for specialty production. The collective’s origin goes back a decade, when Daman, a first-generation coffee producer, visited Nongryniang—a remote village in Khasi Hills and home to the nanny who cared for him in his early years. 

"There, nestled among the misty hills, I came across two old coffee plants growing in someone’s backyard. I later learned that back in the 1980s, the government had briefly launched a coffee planting program in the area. Like many such initiatives, it had long been abandoned and forgotten. But those plants stayed with me. And so did the people.", he recounts. Since then, Daman started a decade-long pursuit of craft and community. From shading systems to post-harvest processing, he spent years learning all it takes to grow high-quality coffee. Over time, the collective has grown in both, resolve and numbers, with 75 farmers now contributing to a harvest. They pick only the ripest cherries by hand, which are sun-dried for 15–22 days depending on weather conditions.  

The first coffee that we’ve sourced from the collective is a natural lot we’ve chosen to roast to a medium profile. It brews cups that open with the aroma of raisins, unfolding into a creamy mouthfeel. Notes of blueberry, black tea, and khasi mandarin carry through in each sip, with a long, marmalade-like finish. A balanced coffee, it lends well to various brewing methods, including espresso, Moka Pot, French Press, and AeroPress. It is enjoyable on its own as well as in milk-based beverages.

Recommended Resting Period: 13 Days

Name: Kolli Berri Estate
Desc:
Our first coffee from Harvest ‘24 is a medium-dark roast with chocolatey and nutty flavours. This single-origin ground coffee hails from the beautiful Kolli Berri Estate, set in Chikmagalur, Karnataka. 

While brewing this one, you’ll notice the unique characteristics of the coffee beans, starting with the aroma of dried fruits, followed by a syrupy mouthfeel in every sip. With medium acidity and medium- high bitterness, it offers a full-bodied profile which is enhanced when brewed as an espresso or using an AeroPress, Moka Pot or a French Press.

Name: Ratnagiri Estate - Dark Room Natural
Desc:
Our latest release from Ratnagiri Estate showcases a new frontier in controlled processing. It was shaped by a 60-hour fermentation with a custom culture, then dried slowly for 13 days in the estate’s climate-controlled dark room.

A rare facility found at only a handful of estates worldwide, the dark room is fully sealed and fitted with precision racks. It holds temperature between 2°C and 30°C and maintains humidity at 10%. Slow drying with this level of control deepens flavour, preserves sweetness, and brings clarity to the cup.

Antony, our roaster, approached the roast with a carefully extended Maillard phase to build natural sweetness, finishing light to let the coffee’s character shine. The result is a sparkling wine-like cup with a silky body and a bright mouthfeel. It opens with the aroma of strawberry and prune. Notes of passionfruit, mosambi, pineapple, and black tea follow, with the tea-like note carrying through the finish.

For the best experience, we suggest brewing this limited-edition lot as a Pour Over or using an AeroPress.

Recommended Resting Period: 8 Days

Name: Kalledevarapura Estate - The Fermentation Edit
Desc:
Meet our roasters’ favourite experiment from Nano-X ’25.

To create this special five-pack, we played with a whole spectrum of microorganisms, from homegrown kombucha to lab-cultured strains. Working with a local laboratory, the producer, Shravan, curated a diverse range of cultures, while Tyler, our Head of Roastery, prepared a robust batch of active kombucha using black tea and raw sugar.

Ripe coffee cherries were split into eleven barrels of 120 kg each, with inoculants gradually added to ten barrels while one was kept as a control. The barrels were sealed and left indoors for a 72-hour fermentation, with the kombucha batch opened after 24 hours to allow oxygen exposure, as the SCOBY (Symbiotic Culture of Bacteria and Yeast) requires it to remain active. Once fermentation was complete, the cherries were dried on raised beds for 20 to 25 days.

This limited-release brings together the highest-scoring samples from the experiment. It includes lots fermented with:

Homegrown Kombucha, creating a cup with notes of plum, raw mango, candy apple, and goji berries.

Saccharomyces cerevisiae, building an expressive coffee with notes of white nectarine, pomegranate, roasted hazelnut, and pomelo.

Pichia yeast, developing a clean cup with notes of cane sugar, green apple, jaggery, and roasted almonds.

Lactic acid bacteria, which shaped a coffee with notes of orange zest, black raisin, wild honey, and cocoa.

An anaerobically processed natural, used to benchmark the inoculated lots. It brews cups with hints of florality and notes of lemonade, roasted almond, and green grape.

We recommend drinking these coffees black, brewed as Pour Overs or using the AeroPress.

Recommended Resting Period: 12 Days

Note: This coffee pack is a special release with limited availability and, therefore, cannot be included in a subscription plan.

Name: Riverdale Estate - White Rose
Desc:
Fermented with rose petals, this layered light roast perfectly embodies why Riverdale Estate is a pioneer in experimental processing.

Only the ripest cherries, hand-picked from the higher-altitude blocks of the farm, where the fruit matures slowly and develops an enhanced sweetness, were used. Once harvested, the cherries underwent a triple wash with natural spring water to remove impurities.

After removing floaters, rose petals were introduced during fermentation, setting up the stage for complexity. The cherries were then slow-dried on raised beds for up to 30 days, allowing for even drying. Finally, the coffee was hulled at the estate’s dry mill, where any defective beans were eliminated before being sent to our roastery.

The result is a gently perfumed cup with bright notes of plum, pomegranate, strawberry and orange blossom, complemented by a smooth mouthfeel and a lingering sweetness.

We recommend brewing it black using an AeroPress or as a Pour Over.

Recommended Resting Period: 14 Days

Note: This coffee pack is a special release with limited availability and, therefore, cannot be included in a subscription plan.

Name: Amruthavarshini Estate
Desc:
Meet our second release by Amruthavarshini Estate, a women-led estate run by a mother-daughter duo. Processed using the anaerobic natural method, this medium roast brews fruity and nutty cups with a pleasant sweetness.  

A honey-like aroma leads into bright notes of cherries and pineapples. The nuttiness of roasted almonds adds depth, while the mouthfeel remains syrupy. In the finish, you’ll taste the lingering aftertaste of raisins and nuts.  

Our roasters recommend brewing it as an espresso, a Pour Over, or using an AeroPress. It tastes great whether you enjoy it black or with milk.

Recommended Resting Period: 12 Days

Name: COZY COOKIE
Desc: Cozy Cookie A washed coffee from Yirgacheffe, Ethiopia, roasted as a balanced omni roast for both filter and espresso. Cozy Cookie is warm, smooth, and comforting by design. Built around sweetness and body rather than acidity, it brings together cocoa, nuts, and soft vanilla notes in a cup that feels familiar and easy. It’s gentle without being boring, sweet without being heavy. Taste Profile Filter Cocoa and roasted nuts lead the cup, followed by soft vanilla sweetness. The profile stays round and smooth with low acidity, finishing clean and cozy with a lingering chocolatey warmth. Espresso Caramel cookie sweetness with a chocolate-forward body. Thick, creamy, and dessert-like, supported by malted vanilla notes and a smooth, lingering finish. Especially good with milk. Brew Recipes V60 Coffee: 15 g Water: 240 ml Ratio: 1:16 Temperature: 92–94°C Grind: Medium Brew Time: 2:30–3:00 Results in a smooth, cocoa-driven cup with gentle sweetness and a calm, comforting finish. Espresso Dose: 18 g Yield: 38–40 g Time: 28–32 seconds Ratio: ~1:2.1 Creamy, chocolatey espresso with caramel cookie sweetness and a rounded mouthfeel. Details Origin: Yirgacheffe, Ethiopia Varietal: Mixed Heirloom Process: Washed Roast: Medium Omni Brew: Filter & Espresso

Name: MOJITO
Desc: This lot from Melkodige Estate is our kind of experiment done right. Ripe SL9 cherries were hand-picked, floated to remove lights, then submerged with EM5 microbes for a 74-hour anaerobic ferment. After that, the cherries were moved to raised wooden trays and dried under shade for 15 days. What this really means is flavor with layers: cocoa and raisin at the core, a lift of sweet lime, and a finish that hints at cacao nib and dried dates. It’s juicy without getting wild, sweet without tasting candy-like. We roast this medium-light to keep the lime sparkle and retain the chocolatey depth that makes the cup feel complete. If you’re into expressive naturals that still behave well on brew bar, this is the one. Taste Cocoa, raisin, sweet lime, cacao nib, dried dates. Brew guide Filter: 1:16, 92–94°C, 2:45–3:00 total (V60/Kalita/AeroPress). Light espresso: 1:2.3 in 30–34s; expect a syrupy shot with citrus pop. Specs Estate: Melkodige Estate, Chikmagalur, KA Variety: SL9 Process: EM5 anaerobic natural (74-hour submerged ferment) Drying: 15 days on raised, shaded beds Elevation: 4200 ft MSL Roast: Medium-Light Best for: Filter, pourover, AeroPress; adventurous light espresso Freshness: Roasted to order. Peak from day 7–28. Reseal tight.

Name: MIDNIGHT EQUATOR
Desc: Midnight Equator A carbonic maceration natural from Uganda, roasted medium to medium-light as a true omni roast. Midnight Equator is precise fermentation done right. The sealed-tank process intensifies fruit clarity while preserving structure, giving the cup layered sweetness without chaos. Dark fruit leads. Cocoa grounds it. The finish lingers long and composed. This is Uganda with control. Taste Profile Filter Black cherry and plum upfront, followed by pomegranate brightness and caramelized sugar sweetness. Cocoa nib undertones add depth, finishing clean, silky, and gently wine-like. Espresso Dense dark chocolate body with stewed berry sweetness. Brown sugar richness supports a rounded acidity and a smooth, lingering finish. Brew Recipes V60 Coffee: 15 g Water: 240 ml Ratio: 1:16 Temperature: 92–94°C Grind: Medium Brew Time: 2:30–3:00 Results in a layered, fruit-driven cup with cocoa depth and refined sweetness. Espresso Dose: 18 g Yield: 38–42 g Time: 28–32 seconds Ratio: ~1:2.1 Thick chocolate body, structured fruit sweetness, long clean finish. Details Origin: Uganda Process: Carbonic Maceration Roast: Medium Omni Brew For: Filter & Espresso Fermented in control. Roasted for clarity. Built for depth

Name: HARBOR MALABAR
Desc: A slow aged coffee shaped by India’s monsoon winds, this Arabica from Chikkamagalur goes through the traditional monsooning process where the beans swell, mellow, and transform in both color and character. The result is a cup that’s incredibly smooth, almost zero in acidity, and deeply grounding. It opens with earthy and woody tones, followed by a soft musty depth that’s unique to monsooned coffees. The finish is mellow, slightly sweet, and comforting in a way only this style can deliver a warm, rugged, and unmistakably Indian. Taste Notes Cocoa Nibs, Nutty, Raisins - with an mellow sweet finish Roast Medium-Dark Variety SLN 795 Process Monsooning Region Chikkamagalur, Karnataka Elevation 1200 MSL

Name: ANAEROBIC NATURALS- AMMIKULAVI ESTATE
Tasting_Notes: PLUM CAKE, LEMON VERBENA, SPICE, STRAWBERRY, CACAO NIBS Best Brewed with: POUR-OVER, AEROPRESS, OR MODERN ESPRESSO Roaster’s Select Recipes: Pour Over: 18G COFFEE, 270ML WATER, MEDIUM GRIND, BREW TIME: 2:30–2:45 Aeropress: 17G COFFEE, 220ML WATER, INVERTED METHOD, BREW TIME: 2 MIN STEEP + 30 SEC PRESS
Desc: FROM THE COOL, ELEVATED LANDSCAPE OF THE PULNEY HILLS IN TAMIL NADU COMES A COFFEE SHAPED BY CAREFUL HANDWORK, CONTROLLED FERMENTATION, AND TIME. THIS IS OUR FIRST COLLABORATION WITH THE AMMIKULAVI ESTATE, LOCATED NEAR KODAIKANAL AT AROUND 1400 MASL, WHERE SLOW CHERRY DEVELOPMENT AND COOL CLIMATES ALLOW FLAVOUR TO FORM WITH DEPTH AND STRUCTURE. THIS MICROL0T IS PRODUCED USING A 72-HOUR ANAEROBIC FERMENTATION, WHERE RIPE, HAND-PICKED CHERRIES ARE SEALED IN AIRTIGHT BARRELS TO DEVELOP SWEETNESS AND COMPLEXITY IN A CONTROLLED, OXYGEN-FREE ENVIRONMENT. FOLLOWING FERMENTATION, THE COFFEE IS WASHED, BRIEFLY SUN-DRIED, AND THEN SHADE-DRIED SLOWLY ON RAISED BEDS. A FINAL RESTING PERIOD ALLOWS THE FLAVOURS TO STABILISE AND INTEGRATE FULLY. IN THE CUP, THIS COFFEE IS LAYERED AND EXPRESSIVE, WITH NOTES OF PLUM CAKE, LEMON VERBENA, WARM SPICE, STRAWBERRY, AND CACAO NIBS. ROASTED MEDIUM-LIGHT, IT MAINTAINS CLARITY AND SWEETNESS WHILE OFFERING A ROUNDED BODY AND STRUCTURED FINISH. THIS IS A COFFEE THAT REFLECTS ITS PROCESS AND PLACE HONESTLY — PATIENT, BALANCED, AND QUIETLY COMPLEX. Desc: This beautiful microlot coffee from Baarbara Estate undergoes a distinctive double fermentation process, combining the benefits of natural and honey processing methods. Initially, the coffee cherries are fermented whole without depulping, allowing the fruit to impart rich, fruity flavors and aromas. After this natural fermentation stage, the pulp is removed, and the coffee undergoes a secondary fermentation with a layer of mucilage intact, characteristic of the honey process. This innovative approach enhances the coffee's complexity, sweetness, and body, resulting in a truly unique flavor profile that showcases the best of both processing worlds. Information: Estate: Baarbara Estate Region: Chikmagalur, Karnataka Producer: Sreeraksha Purnesh Varietal: SL795 (Cross of S288 and the Kent variety, developed by the Central Coffee Research Institute, India) Process: Honey double fermentation Elevation: 3850-5350 feet above sea level Tasting Notes: Red Grape, Cranberry, Melon, Fruit & Nut Choc, Tea like finish Harvest: November to February Best Brewed with: Espresso, Aeropress, French Press, Mokapot, V60 Brew Recipe: Espresso: Dose- 21 grams, Yield- 40 grams, Time- 28-31 seconds V60: Dose- 18 grams, Brew Water Weight- 240 grams, Time- 02:25-02:35

During roasting, we leaned into a medium profile to preserve the coffee’s natural caramel sweetness and creamy milk chocolate body , while carefully stretching the development to bring out the pecan-like nuttiness and a touch of amaretto richness. At the same time, we made sure to protect the bright citrus acidity , so it lifts the cup without turning sharp. The result is a coffee that feels both vibrant and comforting —a daily drinker with enough intrigue to keep you coming back for another sip. It’s not every day you find a coffee where wet coconut and blackcurrant-like notes coexist so naturally—and we knew the roast had to highlight that playful balance. We opted for a medium roast to preserve the juicy brightness of amla and lemon zest while deepening the milk chocolate and spice undertones for a rounded, comforting body. This approach allowed the cup to shine in its contrasts— sweet, tart, creamy, and warm all at once —without tipping too far in any direction. The result is a vibrant yet approachable single origin , crafted for those who enjoy coffees that surprise the palate while staying deeply enjoyable with every sip. Desc: From the forested hills of Nagaland comes a coffee shaped by altitude, patience, and quiet precision. Nagaland Naturals is a rare nanolot from Tsiese Estate, grown in the Kohima district at 1500 MASL, where cool temperatures and shaded canopies allow flavour to develop slowly and distinctly. Processed as an anaerobic natural, ripe cherries are fermented in a sealed, oxygen-free environment, intensifying sweetness while preserving clarity and structure. The result is a cup that feels both comforting and expressive — layered, balanced, and gently vibrant. In the cup, expect vanilla cake and caramel sweetness, followed by strawberry and apricot fruit tones, with a subtle tamarind-like brightness adding lift. Roasted medium-light, this coffee retains its natural character while offering a rounded body and clean finish. This is a coffee that reflects its origin honestly — quiet, complex, and deeply intentional. Information: Estate: Tsiese Estate Region: KOHIMA DISTRICT, NAGALAND Producer: LHOUVILIE YHOR Varietal: SL9 & SL13 Lot: NANOLOT Process: ANAEROBIC NATURALS Roast Level: MEDIUM LIGHT Tasting Notes: VANILLA CAKE, CARAMEL, STRAWBERRY, TAMARIND, APRICOT Harvest: November to February Best Brewed with: POUROVER, AEROPRESS, ESPRESSO Roaster’s Select Recipes: Pour Over – 18g coffee, 270ml water, medium grind, brew time: 2:30–2:45 Aeropress - 17g coffee, 220ml water, inverted method, brew time: 2 min steep + 30 sec press

We slowed down the Maillard stage to deepen its fruit tone, enhancing the natural mulberry and red grape character. A short development sealed in clarity, keeping the cup refined, structured, and true to its fermentation-led complexity. In the cup, it shines with lifted citrus brightness, juicy red fruit depth, and a silky nougat finish. Bold yet delicate, experimental yet balanced — this is a Microlot for those who chase nuance and exceptional processing. Name: Ratnagiri Estate- Rum Barrel Aged
Tasting_Notes: Rum Like, Oak, Caramel, Vanilla Best Brewed With: Espresso, Aeropress, Pour Over, French Press Roaster’s Select Recipes: Espresso: 21g coffee, Brew Time: 28-31 sec Aeropress: 17g coffee, 220ml water, inverted method, Brew Time: 2 min steep + 30 sec press Pour Over: 16g coffee, 250ml water, 3 pours, Brew Time: 2:45 to 3:00
Desc: This Rum Barrel Aged lot from Ratnagiri Estate is unlike anything else we roast. The green coffee spends three months aging in premium rum barrels, slowly absorbing the deep, boozy character of oak, caramel, and vanilla. When it arrived at our roastery, we knew the challenge was to honor the barrel influence without letting it overpower the cup. We landed on a medium-light roast, carefully balancing development to preserve the rum-kissed aromatics while drawing out a silky sweetness in the body. The result is a coffee that opens with rich caramel and oak, unfolds into smooth vanilla warmth, and finishes with a gentle Rum Like-like undertone that lingers on the palate. It’s decadent, layered, and playful—a coffee that blurs the line between tradition and innovation, crafted for those who want an experience as memorable as it is flavorful. Information: Estate: Ratnagiri Estate Region: Chikmagalur, Karnataka Producer: Ashok Patre Varietal: Arabica Catuai Process: Anaerobic Fermented Roast Level: Medium Light Tasting Notes: Rum Like, Oak, Caramel, Vanilla Best Brewed With: Espresso, Aeropress, Pour Over, French Press Roaster’s Select Recipes: Espresso: 21g coffee, Brew Time: 28-31 sec Aeropress: 17g coffee, 220ml water, inverted method, Brew Time: 2 min steep + 30 sec press Pour Over: 16g coffee, 250ml water, 3 pours, Brew Time: 2:45 to 3:00

Name: Tricolate Coffee Brewer
Desc: The Right Conditions for High Extractions Taking inspiration from precision pouring accessories and flat-bed brewers alike, the Tricolate offers more control over flow rate, agitation, and percolation than most brewers and significantly reduces the possibility of channeling. This is achieved by a combination of elements, including the flat bottom and its form-fitting filter, which eliminate bypass, ensuring that all the liquid in the cup after the brew will contain coffee solids; the wide base (80mm in diameter) and vertical walls, which make for a shallow, even coffee bed that creates the ideal conditions for uniform water-coffee contact; and the dispersion screen, which distributes the water evenly, reducing the likelihood of channeling. The result of such a finely tuned brewing system is high extraction, which translates to the palate as dense flavor. Agitation With Minimal Effort An oft-overlooked aspect of pour-over brewing is the pour itself, which has the dual responsibility of evenly saturating and satisfactorily agitating the coffee grounds with the water. Although this sounds easy, it is not, and is most often helped along by a special gooseneck kettle and a steady hand. Tricolate, however, has removed that one variable from the equation. The precision holes in the Tricolate's dispersion screen control the flow rate, dictating how much water can get through at any given time, and the screen itself, mounted roughly four inches above the base, controls the pour height and therefore the agitation. As a result, it is possible to achieve consistently high extractions with minimal effort and with any kettle. All that is required for a perfect brew is the appropriate grind size and water temperature. The Tricolate will do the rest. Environmentally Sound The Tricolate is made in Australia of Tritan plastic, which is durable, heat-stable, and free from BPA, BPS, or other bisphenols. The German-made filters, a bag of which is included in the package, have a consistent pore structure, another reason for the high extractions, and, being relatively small, are made from less paper than those for traditional pour over brewers, reducing the environmental impact of every brew.

Name: OMAKASE VOL. II: WHISPERS AT ORIGIN
Desc: A journey through transformation, fermentation, and the quiet alchemy of craft. Omakase Vol. II invites you into a tasting experience shaped by the forces we rarely see — microbes, time, aroma, and quiet transformation. This edition unfolds as a three-course coffee journey, each course paired with a thoughtfully crafted vegetarian dish designed to mirror the coffee’s mood, process, and sensory arc. Guided by our roasters, guests move through a narrative where flavor is shaped long before the cup: in fermentation, in interaction, in transference. Every chapter reveals a distinct expression of change through temperature, texture, aroma, and ritual. To deepen the experience, this volume features a special international coffee, woven into the tasting arc to introduce a global perspective on process, craft, and origin. Omakase Vol. II is immersive, intentional, and quietly dramatic — a meditation on how the unseen becomes taste.

Desc: After battling the morning hustle at the office, your nerves are rightly calling out for a cuppa. Name: Couverture Canephora - Roasted on 23/02
Desc: Fine Cup Award Winning Process Exclusive Lot. Limited Edition: 16 kgs. Chocolatey, berry-like, boozy, all in the same coffee? Yes, the complexity of this coffee is truly mind boggling! This is the 3rd year of us bringing the Couverture Canephora to you. This beautiful Robusta is grown by Mr Mahesh Nayananan of TheNaturalFarmer, based in Pulneys, Tamil Nadu, and fermented using their proprietary methods. Canephora, an old name of the Robusta, has us coming back for more. This coffee is fruity, acidic, and chocolatey - with zero bitterness, all at the same time! Tasting this coffee is like drinking a light and boozy Madagascar hot chocolate. Isn’t that mind-blowing? This coffee is a limited lot of 16kg , and has won the Flavour of India - Fine Cup Award 2023 for Robusta Naturals. We cupped the first edition of this coffee blind, with 5 people, and none of them could say it was a Robusta. It continues to blow many more minds ever since. The coffee beans that go into Couverture Canephora were nurtured for 17 months - 12 months on the plant, 15 days for fermentation, and 4.5 months, for extended slow drying. The result of so much time, love, effort, and attention is something so complex, it opened our eyes. Coming from sir Mahesh Narayanan and the team at TheNaturalFarmer, this coffee clearly reflects the excellent cultivation practices that the coffee has received during the harvest and beyond, from the nurturing of sapling to plant.

Coming from sir Mahesh Narayanan and the team at TheNaturalFarmer, this coffee clearly reflects the excellent cultivation practices that the coffee has received during the harvest and beyond, from the nurturing of sapling to plant.

Name: Fiano Solaré - Roasted on 23/02
Desc: Citrusy, Orange Zest, Nuts, Almond, Caramel, Floral hints Some choose therapists. But for some, coffee is the therapy. No, not the just cup, but also the plants. Sujay Pradhan, the parent, as we'd like to call him, of this estate, treats this space as his meditation retreat . Intercropping is essential for coffee, and Sujay didn't just handpick the coffee seeds, he also chose what he grew for shade. This estate is rich with mango, lychee, cashew , as well as cardamom , amongst others. He has even put up signs next to the trees, for the visitors to enjoy. And yes, we asked - homestay coming soon! Complex coffees with Orange Zest notes are a favourite, both in pour-overs, and espressos. We chose this lot for the notes, then made sure it was an omniroast. Processed by fermenting this coffee for 36 hours before washing it gives it complexity. It makes for a smooth, enigmatic espresso , and a complex pour-over with slight hints of florals once it cools down. This is our first offering from the Koraput region - a non-traditional area, and it comes from the Brown Valley Coffee Estate.  The Estate is one of the earliest pioneers of specialty-coffee processing in the Koraput valley. Established in 1993, it wasn’t an inheritance passed down through generations—it was a vision built from scratch. What was once an untouched valley was transformed by Sujay Pradhan into a thriving coffee estate, every plant sown with intention, care, and deliberation. Young estates mean rich, fertile soil—and rich, dense coffee beans. Espresso lovers , take note: grind a touch coarser to unlock the full depth of this cup. It makes extremely juicy, oily cups with those signature tiger stripes. It is forgiving in its grind sizes, but fine tuning improves taste and reduces bitterness significantly. We have learnt that grinding coarser works best for dense coffees such as this one.

Name: Maison Mahua - Roasted on 24/02
Desc: Limited Lot of 30kg only. In the hills of Punjisil village, on the banks of the Punjisil Falls , a community of 50 families nurtures this 75 acres of land - 1.5 acres awarded to each beneficiary - an eligible member of the family, harvesting coffee that grows wild among forest cover and stream-fed slopes — where access requires a long, steep walk from the village, and crossing the river stream on foot. Here, harvesting remains a community act, guided by rhythm rather than machinery. Ripe red cherries are hand-carried for over two kilometres, across the river, where they’re de-pulped by a hand-operated pulper, then naturally fermented overnight in the cool, running water of the stream itself. The coffee is then sun-dried on handmade wooden beds, built from locally and seasonally available timber and leaves. Each farmer keeps their parchment at home until moisture is checked and lots are aggregated. Roasted to a medium profile that is suitable for both espresso as well as filter, the resulting cup has a body we fell in love with. It's the kind of cup that you can have everyday, whether as a morning cheer me up, or as a quite wind down at the end of day. Taste Profile Roasted Nuts, Milk Chocolate, Citrus Zest, Vanilla Origin Punjisil, Koraput, Odisha Processing Traditional Washed Elevation 3000+ ft

That it shall be a fruity, boozy, creamy, moody holiday. No barrelly, woody notes. Promise. The espresso shot from this coffee is so balanced, it must be the only Whiskey Aged that can be enjoyed with milk - the kind we make out of medium roasts. It's great with mixers, too! Enjoyable in all the different, versatile brewing methods - this one disappoints in none! Taste Profile Creamy, Caramel, Hints of Irish Whiskey Origin Chikmagalur, Karnataka Processing Whiskey Aged Elevation 3500+ ft

Name: Caffinary Tee

Name: Midnight Fuel - The All-Nighter
Desc: The incredibly competitive world we live in often mandates some extra effort, which usually means burning the midnight oil to stay ahead of the curve. So, get a cup and hustle on!

Name: Pre-Workout - The Punch
Desc: Robustas are an important part of our day - and using them as a pre-workout has been a constant for us. To do this the Award Winning Way, we have partnered with Roesgarden Farming Group - an award winning estate - with a variety so unique, it looks like an Arabica. Name: Prosecco Aventi - Pre-Order Now
Desc: Taste Profile - Winy, Sweet Pickled Lemon, Malt Origin - Koraput A1 Coffee Estate, Koraput, Odisha Varietal - Catimor Processing - Extended Anaerobic Honey, 240 hrs sun-dried, Split beans Elevation - 3200 ft Roast: Medium Acidity: Bright Sweetness: High From award-winning estate - Koraput A1 Estate During harvest, unseasonal rainfall caused a portion of cherries to split — raising the very real risk of farmer losses. Rather than discard them, the lot was carefully segregated and given a second chance through one of the most labour-intensive processes in specialty coffee. Each cherry was manually sorted, floated to remove defects, and sealed into fermentation vessels under oxygen-limited conditions for a full 240 hours — 10 days of controlled anaerobic fermentation, closely monitored to build aromatic complexity without tipping into over-fermentation. Post-fermentation, the cherries were depulped with generous mucilage retained — the honey process — and moved to raised drying beds. Given the compromised skins, drying was managed with frequent turning to ensure even moisture migration. The parchment was then conditioned, rested, and dry-milled to grade. Ten days of patience show up exactly where they should. The cup opens with a winy depth — that unmistakable ferment character that lingers on the sides of your tongue. As it cools, a sweet pickled lemon brightness lifts through, tart but rounded, like a preserved citrus rather than a sharp acid. The finish is long and grounding — malt warmth that settles everything into place. Best brewed slow. Best drunk without distraction.

Name: Riesling Esten - Sold Out
Tasting_Notes: Strong boozy body with layers of purple fruit and bright bergamot at first encounter, mellowing into the sweetness of wild honey . The cup evolves beautifully, revealing the sophisticated tannins of black tea. Taste Profile - Purple Fruit, Bergamot, Wild honey, Black tea, Boozy Origin - TheNaturalFarmer, Pulneys, TN Processing - Extended Fermented, 4.5 Months Slow Dried Elevation - 3600 ft Roast: Medium Acidity: High Sweetness: High We don't recommend this coffee for straight espresso shots or with milk
Desc: Award Winning Coffee. Limited Edition of 16kgs only. Drumroll! The lot that won the Fine Cup Award in 2024 in the Arabica Experimental Category - The Crown Jewel from The Natural Farmer is here. This is a complex Arabica with fruits of labour from the signature long love, care and effort of this estate, not just before, but also post harvest. The S10 varietal is a double cross hybrid of (Caturra x Cioccie) x (Caturra x S.795). Caturra originated in Brazil, Cioccie is of Ethiopian origin, and S795 is a hybrid bred by the Indian Coffee Board. This makes it a complex mix of acidity, body and flavour. This roast balances the complex acidity and sweetness of the coffee. A true masterpiece of patience and precision , the Riesling Esten undergoes an extraordinary extreme fermentation process followed by an unprecedented 4.5-month slow drying period—a testament to the estate's unwavering commitment to excellence. Cultivated at 3600 feet in the pristine Pulney Hills of Tamil Nadu, each cherry is hand-selected through at least 8 meticulous rounds of picking, ensuring only the most perfect fruit makes it to processing. This painstaking attention to detail reveals itself in every sip. With its remarkably low bitterness , this medium roast delivers a vibrant, complex cup - we suggest you bypass it to reveal the full spectrum of this exceptional coffee's character. Tasting Notes: Strong boozy body with layers of purple fruit and bright bergamot at first encounter, mellowing into the sweetness of wild honey . The cup evolves beautifully, revealing the sophisticated tannins of black tea. Taste Profile - Purple Fruit, Bergamot, Wild honey, Black tea, Boozy Origin - TheNaturalFarmer, Pulneys, TN Processing - Extended Fermented, 4.5 Months Slow Dried Elevation - 3600 ft Roast: Medium Acidity: High Sweetness: High We don't recommend this coffee for straight espresso shots or with milk

Name: Robustas of Coorg - Roasted on 18/02
Desc: India is a land of smallholder farmers - and even coffee is grown at estates with less than a ton of production. And do you know what is the smallest quantity that can be graded and sorted in most affordable curing houses? A ton. So while we like the highest grade and best bean density in our coffee, the smallholders who do good work, don't get the limelight that they should, for the hard work they put in. Robusta is a healthy child that has adapted well to climate change, and is soon turning into the highlight of this industry, Worldwide. Bhavika states that she had her biases against robusta - but this is the first coffee ever, that opened her mind to the possibilities that robusta holds in its folds. Bringing to you, a washed Robusta that is sensitive to the Indian small-holders, a roast that bears in mind the qualities of the bean, and brings you, nothing but the best. The coffee will remind you of chocolates, prunes, and raisins. Proudly presenting, Robustas of Coorg. Special thanks to Ujjwal Rathi for ensuring that his love for this coffee and consistent reminders made us stay on track to share this coffee with the rest of the fam. Name: Tawny Ristretta - Roasted on 04/03
Desc: Limited edition of 45kg Fine Robustas have always been close to our hearts, and this one adds yet another layer to our journey of discovering truly exceptional lots. Hegbal Estate gets its name for Hebbagillu - Kannada for "great gateway". R un by Mr Devdas Menezes since 1996, he is a 3rd generational grower who has pioneered specialty harvests and post harvests for both Arabica and Robusta, and believes in a bright future for Robusta. We got our hands on a beautiful bodied batch - an anaerobic Honey fermented twice for 60 hours. The cherries were stored in Ecotact bags, then pulped, and stored in Ecotact bags again. After six months of experimentation and five distinct roast profiles, we’ve arrived at this expression — one that best highlights the character of this coffee. We’re releasing it in a limited batch at a special price to invite your palate into the conversation. Your feedback will shape how we take this coffee forward in future roasts.

Name: Garnet Vin Doux - Roasted on 04/03
Desc: Grown along the outer slopes of the Palani Hills at 4200 ft , this lot represents a precise approach to Robusta processing from Ammikulavi Estate , Tamil Nadu. The estate spans 40 acres, where Arabicas occupy the central terrain and Robustas border the edges. Under the direction of Darshan , a sixth-generation grower and first-generation specialty processor, this coffee undergoes anaerobic natural fermentation —a sealed environment that intensifies fruit complexity while refining mouthfeel and sweetness. When brewed at 89°C for 2 1/2 mins using an AeroPress , the cup reveals a balanced, structured profile: Aromatics: Ferment-driven winey notes with subtle spice Flavor: Winey, D ark chocolate, prunes, and caramel sweetness. Body: Full, syrupy texture with clean finish. Acidity: Low and integrated, enhancing perceived sweetness. Taste Profile - Winey, Dark Chocolate, Prunes, Caramel Origin - Ammikulavi Estate, Pulneys, TN Processing - Anaerobic Naturals Elevation - 4200 ft Roast: Medium Acidity: Low Sweetness: Medium

Name: ROOIBOS TEA  (South African)
Desc: Rooibos tea is made from the leaves of "red bush" plant, which grows only in the small Cederberg region of South Africa. Because it does not derive from the Camillia sinensis plant (like black, white, green or oolong teas), rooibos tea is considered more of an herbal drink or tisane than a "true" tea. Rooibos tea is often called "red tea" or "red bush" tea because of the bright red coloring the leaves take on during the oxidation and fermentation processes. A properly brewed cup of rooibos tea will be a rich red color and have a sweet, nutty flavor.

Name: ROOIBOS TEA  (South African)
Desc: Rooibos tea is made from the leaves of "red bush" plant, which grows only in the small Cederberg region of South Africa. Because it does not derive from the Camillia sinensis plant (like black, white, green or oolong teas), rooibos tea is considered more of an herbal drink or tisane than a "true" tea. Rooibos tea is often called "red tea" or "red bush" tea because of the bright red coloring the leaves take on during the oxidation and fermentation processes. A properly brewed cup of rooibos tea will be a rich red color and have a sweet, nutty flavor.

Name: COLOMBIAN ARABICA COFFEE

Grown at around 2000 metres above sea level, the varieties cultivated are similar to the traditional Yirgacheffe, but with additional local genotypes from plant varieties grown in the forests of the area. This coffee is medium-bodied with outstanding acidity, floral notes and citrus aromas reminiscent of orange and bergamot. Its persistent aftertaste is characterised by hints of fresh fruits and spices. Tasting Notes An elegant example of Ethiopian coffee at its finest, medium bodied with outstanding acidity, Sweet floral aromas combine with tart notes of citrus. When this coffee is in season, everything looks a bit brighter.

Attention to grind size, agitation, and brew time is critical to achieve optimal clarity and balance in the cup. This coffee is a testament to our commitment to innovation and continuous refinement in roasting. The estate and efforts: We all are familiar with the producer Mr. Ashok Patre and his family run estate Ratnagiri Estate. Our founder visited the farm back in the month of march 2021 when coffee processing was at its peak. A day's visit to the estate to understand the farm, the processing techniques and the history behind the legacy was great. Our meeting began with knowing each other and talking and about the passion that runs Grey Soul Coffee as a brand. Then it led to discussions about the specialty community and culture in our country right now. Moving on, we spoke about cup score, Q grading and how it varies from person to person and hence become highly subjective. Then we spoke about international markets and a comparison between Indian and south American coffee. Then quickly moved on a long elaborate your of the farm where some coffee was milled and ready, some drying on raised beds, some drying out in the fields and hand garbling in works as final sorting was in process. In the end, specialty coffee can be simply defined as the coffee that is of the best quality without comprises. This is exactly what this estate stands for and believes in. In the cup, expect ripe banana, deep date sweetness and milk chocolate layered over a subtle melon finish. The body is heavy and syrup like, producing a dense crema and a long, structured aftertaste with balanced acidity. Versatile across brew methods, it performs exceptionally well in milk, where the sweetness expands and the texture becomes velvety and round.
