Name: Anuswaram #6
Desc:
Anuswaram in Carnatic parlance means a note between notes and denotes complex melodic movements that rāga-s tend to employ.

We sometimes recieve small lots that captivate us with either their complexity or innovative processing. We feel Anuswaram is a fitting name for these intriguing coffees.

 For the 6th iteration; we are featuring a very complex arabica natural from Balmaadi estate. The property is nestled high up in the O'valley region of the Nilgiris and is amongst the highest altitude Indian estates growing coffee.  Ably managed by Unnamalai Thiagarajan and team; Balmaadi estate has been one of the pioneers in regenetive agriculture and have been using biodynamic techniques for their coffee and other crops that they grow.

This particular lot is a collaboration with Yettu craft coffee (heralded by Mr. Viggnesh), who have managed the post harvest processing; including a very controlled Anoxic ferment on the naturals. We can't reveal too many details but let's just say the blend of SLn 09 and SLn 795 cherries got a lot of attention over during 72 hours!

 The altitude, microclimate, healthy plants and careful post harvest processing have all conspired to create one of the most complex and elegant naturals that we have encountered! There is oodles of raspberry and mango-esque juciness in the acidity ; a pear like sweetness and hibiscus-ey florals throughout the cup from start to finish. This coffee  is a fruity bonanza that is also very drinkable and crisp tasting. No overwhelming funk here! We had a ball of a time finishing off test batches while profiling the roast  and found it extremely hard to pin this coffee down to three tasting notes. This lot is also our first light roast as we wanted to place the complexity front and centre.

 Anuswaram 6 is a tropical delight across all brew methods 12 days post date of roast (this wait time is critical as the coffee changed dramatically for the better post day 10) and makes for a juicy shot of espresso 22 days post date of roast.

Name: Dēvagāndhāri
Desc:
Last year's floral hit is back!
 
Situated in Chikmagalur, Indravathi estate is the second fully organic farm we have sourced from. It is managed by the same folks who run Narmada estate and boy does the care show in the cup!

 For this lot, cherries have been picked ripe, pulped (i.e the skin being removed) and then dried carefully on raised beds along with the mucilage. The end result of this process is very enjoyable!

 This year's lot is also floral (albeit with less  intensity than last year's lot) but is doubly as juicy  and sweet with the acidity reminding us of Orange pulp and the sweetness of raisins.

 This coffee from Indravathi estate reminds us of the coffee dēvagāndhāri(think of it as ārabhi 's pulpier cousin, musically speaking). 

Dēvagāndhāri the coffee is an absolute delight across all manual brews but shines the most in a no bypass brewer (we use the tricolate), 6 days post roasting. It also makes a pulpy shot of espresso 12 days post date of roast.

 We thank South India Coffee Company for having helping us procure this hidden gem for a second straight year!

Name: Hamīrkalyāni
Desc:
We have a new honey process coffee and it's extra sweet!

Sourced from Krishnagiri estate ,high up in the Chandra drona hills(a.k.a the Giris) of Chikmagalur, this particular lot fascinated us with its sweetness and lingering fruitiness.

Ripe cherries of the SLn. 795varietal have been selected and fermented in 2 stages for 72hours. The coffee is then pulped and slow dried for 10-12 days.

The resulting cup is very sweet and rather interesting;  bursting with cardamom like spice notes . The lychee like tartness reminds us of the rāga Hamīrkalyāni and this coffee is very drinkable( we kept sipping a lot of it during testing).
Hamīrkalyāni the coffee, is a delight across all manual brews 8 days from date of roast  and also makes for a partly sweet ,partly fruity  shot of espresso 16 days from date of roast.

Name: Nalinakānti
Desc:
We have a new coffee from Ram estate and it's a super complex honey! 

 Located in the village of Kamanur near Thandigudi, Ram estate (called Rothaikadu by locals ) posseses a unique microclimate that is idealfor growing complex arabicas  and the folks there  have been processing top notch coffees from year one of their foray into the  speciality scene. The estate has also gone spray-free, with organic inputs being applied directly above the root system instead of being sprayed, helping to reduce runoff.

  This particular lot consists only of  selectively picked SLN 09 arabica from the estate's highest portion. The cherries were fermented in a sealed barrel for 120 hours. They were then pulped and slow dried in a well ventilated polyhouse.

  The resulting cup is very aromatic ,very  citrusy  and very sweet, but also shockingly 'clean' tasting ; without any fermenty notes. This is party a result of the aforementioned microclimate and partly because of careful monitoring of the cherries during fermentation and the slow drying.  The acidity tastes of blood orange and lychee with a lingering raisin like sweetness; reminding us of the rāga Nalinakānti 

Nalinakānti the coffee is a very sweet , complex, sippable brew  and is a delight across all manual brew methods 8 days post roasting. It makes a fruity shot of espresso 16 days post date of roast.

Name: Nātakurinji
Desc:
We super excited to be working with a new farm from the Kodaikanal area this year. Their coffee is quite the flavour bomb!

 Ammikulavi estate is nestled in the upper reaches of the lower Kodaikanal hills and is possesses an ideal climate to grow arabica. 

 For this lot, ripe cherries of the largely caturra varietal( with some SLn 09 and SLN 795) were floated to select for density, sorted once more to select for ultra ripeness and then put in barrels to ferment for 72 hours. The fermentation was carefully monitored and the cherries were then slow-dried on raised beds over 10-14 days. 

 Such meticulous monitoring across all the steps have made this coffee a fruity delight with the intensity dialled upto 11! We taste a bengal currant like acidity , chocolatey sweetness(think of 50% cacao chocolates) and a mild booziness which is tied together with a very prominent rose like aroma.

The overt fruitiness reminded our roaster of the rāga Nātakurinji. Nātakurinji the coffee is a punchy delight across all manual brews 5 days post date of roast and makes for a part fruity part chcoclatey espresso 14 days post roast.

Name: Tōdi
Desc:
Our bold dark roast is back!

Sourced from Krishnagiri estate ,high up in the Chandra drona hills(a.k.a the Giris) of Chikmagalur, this lot of washed arabica fascinated us with its bean density and versatility(traits we have come to associate with the coffee from Krishnagiri estate).

Ripe cherries of the Chandrigiri varietal have been selected for this lot and the estate has tweaked their standard washed process to eke more out of the coffee.

Just like last year, we decided to a more developed roast apart from the medium roast; taking the beans close to second crack but stopping short of that that point. This makes the coffee stand up to milk better but retains some origin character.

The boldness of this coffee reminds us of the rāga tōdi and is our go to for milk based drinks.

Tōdi the coffee is a delight on the espresso machine(10 days post date of roast ) moka pot , south-indian filter and immersion brewers like French press and Aeropress.

Name: THE DREAMER
Desc: An 80:20 Arabica–Robusta blend crafted for those who chase ideas and sip between dreams. This premium blend brings together the smooth richness of Arabica Washed and Naturals with the bold depth of Robusta Washed and Naturals. Balanced, full-bodied, and aromatic—The Dreamer is your perfect companion, whether you're lost in thought or wide awake with ambition.

Name: THE REBEL
Desc: Grown between 1200–1700 MASL, The Rebel is a bold expression of defiance in a cup. A blend of high-grown washed Arabica and honey sun-dried Arabica, this coffee balances clarity with complexity—bright, juicy acidity meets smooth sweetness with a wild streak. Crafted for the nonconformist palate, it’s the brew that refuses to follow the rules.

Name: WHISKEY BARREL AGED | SAKLESHPUR  | ARABICA | FILTER ROAST | 250 GMS
Desc: Indulge in the rich, smoky notes of our Whiskey Barrel Aged Coffee, a seasonal treat that’s perfect for coffee and whiskey lovers alike! Aged to perfection in whiskey barrels, this coffee boasts deep, layered flavors that warm your soul.

Name: RATNAGIRI ESTATE | CHIKMAGALUR | ARABICA | OMNI ROAST | 250GMS
Desc: From the birthplace of Indian coffee, Chikmagalur comes this renowned Ratnagiri coffee. Its cherries are de-pulped and undergo a highly controlled 90-hour extended carbonic-washed-maceration process aimed at extracting the utmost complexity of flavours. Experience the notes of peach, black currant, and mandarin that lead to a gratifying, grapy finish.

Name: THE THINKER
Desc: Rooted in clarity, brewed for contemplation. The Thinker is a thoughtful blend of premium Arabica Washed and Arabica Naturals, grown at 1100–1300 MASL. Smooth, nuanced, and delicately layered—it’s a cup that unfolds slowly, just like a good idea. Made for quiet moments, deep thoughts, and everything in between.

Name: DKAF
Desc: No buzz, all brilliance. The DKAF is a decaf that doesn’t compromise—grown at 1400–1700 MASL and omni roasted for versatility across brew methods. Smooth, mellow, and surprisingly complex, it delivers full flavor minus the caffeine. Perfect for late nights, slow mornings, and mindful sips.

Welcome to the Coffee Learning Community (CLC) Where Curiosity Meets Craft At CLC, we believe that coffee is more than just a beverage—it’s a bridge between people, cultures, and possibilities. Founded with the vision of nurturing a deeper understanding of coffee from seed to cup, the Coffee Learning Community is a space for growers, roasters, baristas, and enthusiasts to connect, share, and grow together. Whether you’re just beginning your journey or seeking to deepen your craft, CLC offers hands-on experiences, expert-led workshops, and collaborative learning opportunities designed to inspire and empower. Rooted in sustainability, quality, and inclusivity, our community brings together passionate individuals who care deeply about the future of coffee. From soil health to sensory analysis, from fermentation techniques to roasting mastery, every session is crafted to expand knowledge and celebrate the people behind each bean. Come learn, taste, question, and create with us. Because great coffee starts with great learning.

Coffee Collection 2024–2025 A Journey in Every Cup Welcome to the 2024–2025 edition of our Coffee Collection. Our story began in 2008, in a small village near Pondicherry, with a simple dream: to roast exceptional Indian coffees, one small batch at a time. With little more than a passion for flavour and a vision for quality, the first roasts were crafted by hand—humble beginnings that sparked a journey of discovery, dedication, and craftsmanship. Seventeen years later, that same spirit continues to guide us. This year’s collection celebrates the full spectrum of coffee—from minty, full-bodied Vienna roasts to bright and delicate light-roasted single estates. Whether you’re seeking a comforting breakfast blend, an intense espresso, or a rare micro-lot, each coffee is a reflection of our unwavering commitment to quality, traceability, and flavour. Every bean carries a story. In every roast a mindful act. May the coffee spirit be with you.

Name: Barista Enhancement : 3-Day Hands-On Training Program
Desc: Introduction This program emphasizes practical learning with espresso machines, grinders, and various manual brewing equipment. Theory is kept minimal, but participants receive a comprehensive PDF to review at home and revisit key concepts covered during the sessions. Description Barista Enhancement is a focused three-day hands-on training program designed for beginners and aspiring café owners, building a solid foundation in coffee preparation and customer engagement. The curriculum thoroughly covers espresso theory and practice, including dialing in the perfect shot, understanding grind size and dosage, and identifying critical factors influencing espresso quality. Milk texturing and frothing skills are included, teaching how to create smooth microfoam and proper steaming techniques essential for quality espresso-based drinks and latte art. Emphasis is placed on equipment care and maintenance to ensure hygiene and optimal espresso machine performance. Participants master practical espresso recipes and efficient workflow management from grind to cup. A core element is understanding roast profiles and how varying roasting stages impact flavor and extraction. Precision tools such as micron scales for particle size analysis, refractometers to measure extraction yield, PPM meters to assess water quality, and analysis of particle size distribution are introduced to optimize extraction quality. The program includes popular manual brewing methods and equipment like Cold Brew, Vacuum Siphon, French Press, Moka Pot, Chemex, V60, and Aeropress, reflecting their growing consumer admiration. Crucially, the training develops baristas’ ability to deeply understand customer preferences, combining historical coffee knowledge with current industry trends to enhance service and foster loyalty. The program equips participants not only with technical expertise but also with customer-centric skills essential for specialty coffee industry success. Name: Barista Essentials Workshop
Desc: Barista Essentials is a 4-hour comprehensive crash course combining foundational espresso knowledge with milk beverage insights and hands-on practice. The first 3 hours cover the anatomy of espresso, key variables affecting extraction, practical methods for evaluating shot quality in real time, core techniques for consistently excellent espresso—including how different post-harvest processing methods influence extraction and flavor—and demonstrations of five core milk-based drinks (Café Latte, Cappuccino, Flat White, Café Cortado, and Espresso Macchiato), highlighting differences in espresso ratios, milk texture, and pouring technique for optimal flavor, balance, and mouthfeel. The final hour provides hands-on practice in milk preparation techniques—such as steaming and texturing milk—and latte art, introducing basic foundations like simple pouring methods, milk steaming for smooth microfoam, and foundational patterns like the heart, with essential steps including controlling pour height and flow, cup angle, and pitcher movement to build confidence in fundamental skills. This course is ideal for keen learners who want to explore the vast universe of espresso in a nutshell or for anyone looking to update and refresh their coffee knowledge. Name: Ratna Raga

Desc: The first phrase that graced the lips of our Q-Grader when she analyzed this coffee was – “Bold and Beautiful.” By pushing this roast into medium dark territory, we get a lovely plethora of dark chocolate notes harmoniously dancing with nutty aromas and a rounded cedar finish. It is ideal for espresso brewing but is sure to be a favourite for Moka Pot enthusiasts and French Press fanatics who love a bold cup with a classic taste profile.

Name: Grind Size Chart
Desc: The Chandragiri varietal when put through the washed process is characterized by clean and bright acidity complemented by nutty and tangy notes and a very subtle floral aroma. This coffee comes from one of our earliest producer partners – Balanoor Plantations – who are pioneers of washed coffees in India and have been exporting some of the finest Arabicas to specialty markets in Europe for several decades.

Name: Grind Size Chart
Desc: With a delicate combination of silky texture, bright citrus blossom notes, and hints of honeydew melon and golden raisins, this coffee yields a truly memorable cup. The dedication and commitment of Mr. Ashok Kuriyan and his son Rohan are evident in every cup. As old friends and long-time collaborators, we have always enjoyed visiting their farms, working with them, and roasting their delightful coffees.

Name: Grind Size Chart
Desc: Berry Dawn from Baarbara Estate is a fruity coffee with sweet jammy notes and an intriguing berry profile that captures the essence of natural processing.

Name: Grind Size Chart
Desc: Our search for the immaculate espresso began when we were embraced by the warm welcome of Ramdev and his parents Shantha and Nagesh as we drove through the gates of Bettadamalali Estate in early 2023. A pristine farm nestled in the Baba Budan Giri hills of Chikmagalur, this place is more than a commercial operation – it is a garden of nature’s best delights. With scientific approaches to farming complemented by highly structured operations, Bettadamalali produce some of the best washed Arabicas we have encountered in recent times. The farm has been a long-term partner to our sister enterprise Indcaffe – who have over the years exported several hundreds of tons of washed Arabica for them to specialty houses in Europe. We decided to grab our own little share of the treasure as we cycled through multiple lots to find this gem that would help us curate a delicious espresso.

Name: Grind Size Chart
Desc: Our first lot from BEWILD Coffee is an anoxic-fermented Fine Robusta from Poomaale Estate. This unique and complex wild-harvested canephora coffee embodies the essence of its origin. It is a testament to nature's resilience and the power of regenerative agriculture. BEWILD have worked closely with a team of growers, roasters, and brewers to cultivate this coffee in a sustainable and ethical way, embracing the principles of permaculture and biodiversity conservation. The result is a distinct coffee experience that celebrates the wildness of the forest and the magic of nature.

Desc: In collaboration with the skilled producers at Harley Estate, nestled in the picturesque region of Sakleshpur, renowned for its rich volcanic soil and unique microclimate, we proudly present India’s famed Robusta Kaapi Royale. This exquisite coffee showcases a perfect harmony of flavor and aroma. Meticulously handpicked at peak ripeness, only the finest Robusta beans are selected, guaranteeing an unparalleled level of quality and consistency.

Name: Grind Size Chart
Desc: The superstar coffee that lit up our roster for many years is finally back—and it’s here to elevate your brewing game. Floral, wild, and crisp with juicy acidity, our latest washed lot from Idido, Yirgacheffe (pronounced yeer-ga-CHUFF-eh) in Ethiopia meets all the high expectations we typically set for Ethiopian coffees. If you’re weary of funky fermentations and on the lookout for clean cups that showcase the unique character of terroir, this coffee is sure to become your muse. We’ve settled on a light to medium roast that ensures the inherent terroir shines through, while the cup boasts enough sweetness to keep you musing—and coming back for more.

Name: Baarbara Estate-HSD
Desc: Honey sun-dried coffee is a beautifully balanced processing style where the coffee cherries are de-pulped but dried with part of the sticky, sweet mucilage still clinging to the beans. As they dry slowly under the sun, this natural sweetness infuses into the seeds, creating a cup that is smooth, syrupy, and vibrant. Expect flavours of ripe fruit, caramel-like sweetness, and a round, creamy body, all while maintaining a gentle acidity. This method highlights both the terroir and the careful craftsmanship of the producer making honey sun-dried coffees a favourite in the speciality world. Name: Basan Khan Estate
Desc: The Basankhan Estate is a family-owned farm located in Chikmagalur, Karnataka with a rich history spanning over 100 years. It was originally founded by their great grandfather, Mr. Gulamenabi, and subsequently managed by G. Abdul Wajid & Sons. Now in its fourth generation, the estate continues to flourish.After picking cherries from the trees, the farm initiates immediate processing. Unwanted cherries are removed, and the coffee is meticulously cleaned with water. A pulping machine is then used to remove the outer layer of the cherries, after which the washed coffee is soaked in water for 12 hours before being transferred to the drying yard.The focus of the Basankhan Estate is to consistently produce the finest beans from their crop. They prioritise thorough washing by performing the process twice. The drying methods employed include mat drying, shade drying, regular drying, and more. During the drying process, careful attention is paid to rotation, ensuring equal drying by turning the coffee every hour. Flavour – Caramel, Citrus, Gooseberry Roast Level – Medium Acidity Level – Medium Bitterness Level – Low Body – Medium Altitude – 1450 MASL Processing – Washed Varietal – SLN 795 Location -Chikmagalur

Desc: The coffee cherries for this microlot are cultivated at mid-elevation slopes of Harley Estate, located in the fertile Chikmagalur region of Karnataka. Name: Monsoon Malabar
Desc: Monsoon Malabar is one of India’s most legendary coffee styles born along the Malabar Coast, shaped by nature, and cherished for its unmistakable flavour. Originally discovered when wooden-hulled ships carried Indian coffee to Europe, the beans would swell, mellow, and transform during the long sea voyages through the monsoon winds. Today, this naturally occurring phenomenon is carefully recreated in controlled warehouses along the coast. Exposed to moist monsoon winds for several weeks, the beans undergo a slow, deliberate transformation: their colour turns pale gold, their size nearly doubles, and their acidity softens beautifully. The result is a bold, smooth, and earthy cup with notes of spice, wood, cocoa, and a gentle sweetness, finishing with a low-acid, rounded body that makes it perfect for espresso and milk-based drinks. At Roastery Coffee House, our Monsoon Malabar celebrates India’s heritage an ode to tradition, craftsmanship, and the unique terroir of the Western Ghats. Rich, comforting, and unmistakably Indian. Name: Iceberg Naturals
Tasting_Notes:
Haw Flakes, Plum Blossom, Persimmon, Mango
Acidity: Malic
Body: Medium
Aftertaste: Long

Size - 250gm / 1kg
Desc:
Iceberg, Our final limited release of the year, crafted to mark the close of 2025 with something truly special. This exceptional coffee embodies a meticulous, hands-on approach to quality that elevates it beyond the ordinary.

Starting its journey at Riverdale Estate, Yercaud in Tamil Nadu, each cherry is carefully hand-picked where slower maturation enhances sugar content and mucilage density, key aspects of natural process coffee. The processor ensure only the ripest cherries move forward, using a Brix meter to measure sugar levels precisely.

Once harvested, the cherries undergo a thorough triple wash using natural spring water from its own estate to remove impurities, followed by a floating process to eliminate underdeveloped beans. The highest-density cherries are fermented with the addition of rose petals, enhancing the development of flavonoids and bringing out cleaner, brighter fruit notes along with a unique floral character.

After fermentation, the cherries are slow-dried on raised beds for up to 30 days, promoting even drying and improved air circulation. This careful process ensures a vibrant, clean cup. The coffee is hulled in our dry mill, where our quality control team meticulously hand-picks any defective beans. To maintain maximum freshness, all our natural process coffees are vacuum-sealed to preserve moisture levels between 11–13%.

Roasted to perfection by our head roaster, Baninder Kochar, Iceberg coffee is profiled for a clean, balanced cup that highlights delicate exotic florals, complemented by Savorworks’ signature long, lingering aftertaste. Expect bright, clean flavors with tasting notes of hawflakes (nostalgic Chinese confection), plum blossom, persimmon, and mango.

Facts:
Estate: Riverdale Estate
Process: Iceberg Naturals
Varietal: SLN9 &  5B
Altitude: 1450 MASL

Feels:
Tasting Notes: Haw Flakes, Plum Blossom, Persimmon, Mango
Acidity: Malic
Body: Medium
Aftertaste: Long

Size - 250gm / 1kg

Name: Coffee Drip Kit - Nutty & Chocolaty
Desc:
Introducing the Savorworks Coffee Drip Kit—expertly crafted for both coffee enthusiasts and first-time black coffee explorers who crave authentic, natural flavors from an excellent brew. Say goodbye to bitterness and embrace a delightful coffee experience that highlights nutty undertones and luscious chocolatey notes, all without the need for sugar. For those who prefer a creamier texture, it’s also delightful with a pour of milk.

This innovative drip kit features specialty Arabica coffee sourced from the renowned Riverdale Estate, roasted and ground to perfection. Enjoy the same remarkable quality as manual pour-over brewing, but with added convenience—no kettles, thermometers, grinders, or scales required. Simply unfold the filter, pour hot water, and savor a beautifully classic black coffee in just a few minutes.

Features:

  • Premium Ingredients: 100% Specialty Arabica Coffee, nitrogen-flushed to lock in freshness.
  • Origin: Sourced from the esteemed Riverdale Estate.
  • Roast Profile: Medium dark roast for a rich, robust flavor with nutty undertones and luscious chocolatey notes.
  • Versatile Enjoyment: Perfect as a black coffee or with a splash of milk for added creaminess.
  • Convenient Packaging: Each kit includes 5 individual 12g servings (60g total), perfect for on-the-go brewing.
  • Storage Tips: Preserve freshness by storing in a cool, dry, and dark place.

Unlock the world of flavorful black coffee with the Savorworks Coffee Drip Kit—your gateway to an enjoyable and rich coffee journey wherever life takes you. Perfect for any setting, this kit ensures that you can appreciate the craft of coffee making effortlessly. Enjoy your coffee, your way!

About Project Pearl



In the Indian Specialty Coffee Industry, the name Ratnagiri Estate evinces a recognition of steadily elevating excellence, innovation, and a devotion to sustainability. The name Ratnagiri itself, translates to pearl mountain.


Over the years, Ratnagiri Estate's legacy in the Indian specialty coffee industry has steadily elevated as the flagbearers of specialty coffee growing, processing, and Indian specialty coffee representation overseas.


Today we’re honoured to be able to tell their story in the fullness of their legacy, with Project Pearl — a microlot program featuring 8 microlots from Ratnagiri Estate, exclusive only to Subko, that showcase the high-scoring, experimentally processed coffees that are a testament to their humble beginnings.

About the Process

84 Hours Yeast Inoculated Natural : The coffee undergoes a meticulous process beginning with selective harvesting—only ripe cherries are hand-picked, sometimes using ladders—and cleaned via flotation to remove low-density beans and debris. The cherries then undergo 84 hours of carbonic maceration fermentation, inoculated with Saccharomyces cerevisiae yeast to enhance flavor. After fermentation, the coffee is dried in a polyhouse, then moved to raised beds and raked regularly for even drying. Once moisture reaches 11–12%, the beans are carefully bagged for storage.

 

About the Roast

Medium Roast : At Subko, a Medium roast is one that is obtained by dropping the coffee lot at 201°-204°C. These roasts are generally of a sensory profile that is very smooth, caramel and complex tropical fruits. In terms of the Agtron scale, Subko's definition of medium lies between the points 60 to 74, with 74 being the lightest version of a medium roast, and 60 being the darkest version of the roast.

About Subko VLGE: Co-operative Agriculture

A sustainable, farm-to-table-to-farmer operation by Subko

Founded by Subko Specialty Coffee Roasters and Craft Bakehouse, the Subko Co-op initiative finds its roots in the village of K. Thadiputtu in Andhra Pradesh. Concentrating its efforts on the holistic advancement of the 'Subko Village,' Subko Co-op has adopted a cluster comprising six tribal farmers from K. Thadiputtu village in Paderu, Andhra Pradesh. With a dedication to bringing these individuals to the forefront of the third wave of coffee, Subko Co-op seeks to not only empower these farmers but to also nurture growth within their entire community.

This initiative is focused on tribal farmers who cultivate coffee on government-allotted lands. With an attention on driving direct trade, sustainability, and hyper-traceability, the initiative embodies a commitment to elevating the agricultural landscape in the world of coffee. This endeavor aims to adopt more such clusters in the future. Furthermore, Subko Co-op envisions the establishment of training centers, designed to empower and educate both farmers and their families, paving the way for them to become coffee professionals and authentic representatives of their cultural legacy and heritage. Subko Co-op’s objective is to emerge as a transformative force, reshaping the narrative of coffee cultivation by amalgamating sustainable practices, cultural preservation, and community empowerment, and to narrate origin stories and recognise every stakeholder who puts their heart in coffee cultivation.

About the Process

Traditional Naturals: 

In this traditional natural process, ripe coffee cherries are harvested and dried whole, with the skin and pulp left intact. As they dry, sugars and fruit compounds slowly ferment and infuse into the bean. The cherries are spread across patios or raised beds and turned regularly to prevent defects, until they reach a stable moisture level for hulling. This method produces coffees with a heavier body, greater sweetness, and pronounced fruity or wine-like character.

About the Roast

Medium Roast : At Subko, a Medium roast is one that is obtained by dropping the coffee lot at 201°-204°C. These roasts are generally of a sensory profile that is very smooth, caramel and complex tropical fruits. In terms of the Agtron scale, Subko's definition of medium lies between the points 60 to 74, with 74 being the lightest version of a medium roast, and 60 being the darkest version of the roast.

Espresso Roast: Espresso Roasts are characterized by their deep, rich flavour profile , often with sweeter, intense notes. The beans are roasted to an espresso roast to bring out their bold flavor , which pairs beautifully with milk.

Processes: Pichia Yeast Naturals + Anaerobic Naturals

Pichia Yeast Naturals: LOT P3-2

This lot underwent a 60-hour anaerobic natural fermentation. Coffee cherries (Brix: 24.6) were depulped after floater removal and placed in bio-fermenters with lab-grown microbes isolated from the farm, inside a nitrogen-rich environment. After fermentation, the cherries went through vacuum impregnation, where it was exposed to 600 millibars of vacuum for 12 hours, followed by instantaneous release. Post which they were transferred to raised drying beds and slow-dried with constant stirring over 30 days.

Anaerobic Naturals: LOT IP-01

This lot underwent an 84-hour extended yeast fermentation. Coffee cherries (Brix: 25.6) were placed in bio-fermenters after floater removal. A strain of Pichia yeast was added, and fermentation took place in a carbon dioxide-rich environment. After fermentation, the cherries were moved to raised beds for slow drying, stirred regularly over 27 days to ensure uniform moisture loss.


About Project Pearl



In the Indian Specialty Coffee Industry, the name Ratnagiri Estate evinces a recognition of steadily elevating excellence, innovation, and a devotion to sustainability. The name Ratnagiri itself, translates to pearl mountain.


Over the years, Ratnagiri Estate's legacy in the Indian specialty coffee industry has steadily elevated as the flagbearers of specialty coffee growing, processing, and Indian specialty coffee representation overseas.


Today we’re honoured to be able to tell their story in the fullness of their legacy, with Project Pearl — a microlot program featuring 8 microlots from Ratnagiri Estate, exclusive only to Subko, that showcase the high-scoring, experimentally processed coffees that are a testament to their humble beginnings.

Filter Roast: Manual brewing methods fall under the artisanal brewing style of coffee. Roasting a coffee is also an art, we have developed this filter roast to maintain the quality while brewing over Pour over, Kalita, V60, Origami, April, Chemex.

About The Process:

Ripe S795 cherries are selectively handpicked and fermented for 60 hours under partially anaerobic conditions, then dry-pulped. The parchment, with mucilage intact, is initially sun-dried on trays before being transferred to the drying yard. Throughout drying, the coffee is raked hourly to ensure uniform airflow, prevent over-fermentation, and maintain consistency, until a final moisture content of 10.5-11% is reached.

About the Process

Naturals: 

Ripe cherries are handpicked, with defects removed, and a sample lot is taken to measure Brix (27). Floaters and foreign material are removed, followed by de-stoning and double washing, before the cherries are placed in double-walled stainless steel tanks and anaerobically fermented for 96 hours with regular monitoring. Post-fermentation, the coffee is dried on raised beds in a greenhouse and raked hourly to maintain temperature and ensure even drying.

Name: Tulum Brew Stick – A Tool to Better your Pour-Over Game | Glass | 1 Pc
Desc: Tulum Brew Stick – Elevate Your Pour-Over Ritual A sleek, functional tool designed to enhance your pour-over brewing experience. The Tulum's Glass Brew Stick helps refine extraction, improve water flow, and create a more balanced, flavorful cup. Why You’ll Love It: Better Extraction – Creates a dip in the coffee bed for even water flow. Even Distribution – Prevents channeling and enhances consistency. Improved Bloom – Puffs up the grounds for optimal saturation. Gentle Agitation – Helps with degassing and uniform brewing. Using the Tulum Brew Stick, create a gentle spiral-shaped divot in the coffee grounds, starting from the outer edge and working inward. This method helps water reach all the grounds evenly, ensuring a more uniform extraction and a well-balanced brew. Key Features: The Perfect Size: lightweight, comfortable and easy to handle. Easy to Clean: Rinse under water or wipe with a damp cloth. Durable Design: Made to withstand regular use without wear and tear. Minimalist Aesthetic: A stylish addition to any coffee brewing setup. Desc: The Blend Bundle Crafted. Balanced. Bold. For the coffee drinker who appreciates the craft of the "perfect profile." The Blend Bundle brings together our three signature house blends: Lumen, Saigon, and Swell. Each one is a unique recipe of beans from different altitudes and estates, roasted specifically to bring out a harmonious, multi-layered experience. From the bright clarity of a morning pour-over to the creamy richness of a traditional milk coffee, this bundle is a masterclass in balance. What’s Inside: 1.The Smooth Operator: Swell Blend (Medium Roast) - The Vibe: Perfectly balanced and incredibly smooth. Like a steady wave, it’s reliable and easy-going. Tasting Notes: Rich Milk Chocolate, Toasted Almonds, and a hint of Caramel. The Cup: This is our most versatile blend. It has enough body to handle milk but is smooth enough to drink black. It’s the "crowd-pleaser" that fits any brewing method. The Blend: A harmonious marriage of washed and natural process beans for a rounded mouthfeel. 2. The Deep Soul: Saigon Blend (Medium-Dark Roast) The Vibe: Bold, nostalgic, and incredibly rich. Inspired by the intense, chocolatey coffee culture of Southeast Asia. Tasting Notes: Heavy Dark Cocoa, Roasted Nuts, and a Smoky Sweetness. The Cup: Thick and syrupy. This blend was born to be paired with condensed milk or frothed milk. If you love a coffee that actually tastes like coffee through the milk, this is it. The Blend: A robust, high-energy blend designed for strength and depth. 3. The Bright Light: Lumen Blend (Light-Medium Roast) The Vibe: Elegant and uplifting. Designed to be your "lightbulb moment" in the morning. Tasting Notes: Delicate Floral notes, bright Citrus, and a sweet Honey finish. The Cup: Our most vibrant blend. It’s clean and crisp, making it the perfect choice for AeroPress, Chemex, or a refreshing iced coffee. The Blend: A curated mix of high-altitude Arabicas that emphasize acidity and sweetness. Why Choose the Blend Bundle? Versatility : Three distinct profiles that cover everything from black coffee to lattes. Consistency: Our blends are crafted to taste great every single time you brew. The Full Spectrum: Experience the progression from light/floral to dark/chocolatey.

Watermelon Fermented Inspired by innovative fermentation techniques , our Watermelon Fermented Coffee is crafted at the Baarbara Estate using only fresh watermelon pulp to highlight the fruit’s bright, juicy character. This medium-roast, 100% Arabica coffee delivers an exhilarating cup that’s as refreshing as it is complex. Flavour Profile Chocolate Truffles → Deep, rich cocoa sweetness Almonds & Cashews → Warm, roasted-nut undertones Dry Fruits → Subtle texture of raisin and fig Mellow Sweetness → Silk-like finish that rounds out the cup Origin & Process Location: Bababudangiri, Chikmagalur Process: Watermelon Fermented (coffee cherries co-fermented with ripe watermelon pulp) Altitude: 3,850–5,350 ft Roast & Brew Roast Level: Medium + roast Perfect For: Espresso, Cold Brew, French Press or Moka Pot Allow your beans to degas for 8–10 days after roasting to develop and settle the nuanced chocolate-nut flavours. Over time, the cup will reveal layers of truffle-like richness, roasted-nut warmth and a gentle, lingering sweetness. *No added sugar, honey, fruit, flavour, chicory, or preservatives. Tulum® – Specialty Coffee Roasters

Flavour Profile Chocolate Truffles → Deep, rich cocoa sweetness Almonds & Cashews → Warm, roasted-nut undertones Dry Fruits → Subtle texture of raisin and fig Mellow Sweetness → Silk-like finish that rounds out the cup Origin & Process Location: Bababudangiri, Chikmagalur Process: Watermelon Fermented (coffee cherries co-fermented with ripe watermelon pulp) Altitude: 3,850–5,350 ft Roast & Brew Roast Level: Medium + roast Perfect For: Espresso, Cold Brew, French Press or Moka Pot Allow your beans to degas for 8–10 days after roasting to develop and settle the nuanced chocolate-nut flavours. Over time, the cup will reveal layers of truffle-like richness, roasted-nut warmth and a gentle, lingering sweetness. *No added sugar, honey, fruit, flavour, chicory, or preservatives.
